patterns.name: Robot bring-up boilerplate: AdvantageKit + PathPlanner warmup + disabledInit stop-everything
patterns.whatItDoes: The `Robot` constructor does `Logger.recordMetadata(...)`, `Logger.addDataReceiver(new WPILOGWriter())`, `Logger.addDataReceiver(new RLOGServer(5810))`, `Logger.start()`, starts the deploy WebServer, constructs RobotContainer, then `CommandScheduler.getInstance().schedule(FollowPathCommand.warmupCommand())` to avoid the first-path JIT stutter. `RobotContainer.disabledInit()` manually calls stop on every mechanism.
patterns.whereSeen: A/Robot.java lines 44-71 and 369-374 of RobotContainer.java; B/Robot.java lines 44-70 and 343-347 of RobotContainer.java. Differ only in the two metadata strings, one `CameraServer.startAutomaticCapture()` (B), and one `DriverStation.silenceJoystickConnectionWarning(true)` (A).
patterns.libraryValue: A `PumpkinRobot extends LoggedRobot` base could take a project name + robot name and do all of it, including the RLOG-on-5810-because-5800-is-taken detail (a real, documented gotcha). `disabledInit()` stop-everything should be a registry (`PumpkinLib.onDisable(subsystem::stop)`) rather than a hand-maintained list that silently rots when a subsystem is added.

patterns.name: Reusable, pre-allocated swerve requests + identical driver binding block
patterns.whatItDoes: Four `SwerveRequest` fields (`FieldCentric drive`, `SwerveDriveBrake brake`, `PointWheelsAt point`, `RobotCentric forwardStraight`) allocated once with `.withDriveRequestType(DriveRequestType.Velocity)` and a 20% deadband, then bound: A=brake, B=point-at-stick, four D-pad `whileTrue` nudges at ±0.5 m/s, four back/start + X/Y SysId combos, left-bumper `seedFieldCentric()`, and the Y-toggle for vision tracking keyed off `aprilTagTrackingCommand.isScheduled()`.
patterns.whereSeen: A/RobotContainer.java lines 96-106 + 180-253; B/RobotContainer.java lines 80-90 + 154-224. Identical except the translation scale (A `* 0.25` for driver practice, B `* 0.75`) and B wrapping the Y-toggle in `if (VisionConstants.LIMELIGHT_NAMES.length > 0)`.
patterns.libraryValue: ~90 lines of identical binding code. PumpkinLib should offer a `DriverBindings.standard(controller, swerve, config)` that installs the whole default set with a configurable translation scale and nudge speed, so a robot's RobotContainer only contains what is actually robot-specific. The `isScheduled()`-based toggle with `finallyDo` cleanup is a genuinely good pattern worth encoding as `Trigger.toggleCommand(cmd)`.

patterns.name: Absolute-encoder-as-truth with guarded re-seeding of the motor sensor (A only)
patterns.whatItDoes: The REV Through Bore (read as a raw `DutyCycle` on DIO 0) is the angle reference. The TalonFX rotor is seeded from it at startup, again immediately before every `setPivotAngle` move, and re-synced from `periodic()` ONLY when neither position nor manual control is active (re-seeding mid-move shifts the reference frame and makes the arm land off target). Connection is detected via `throughBore.getFrequency() > 0` with automatic fallback to the motor sensor. The offset delta is wrapped with `delta -= range * Math.round(delta / range)` so it is stateless and safe for multiple readers.
patterns.whereSeen: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/9143-2025-A-Updated/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/CorAl.java lines 121-125, 190-223, 286-344, 405-407.
patterns.libraryValue: A textbook `AbsoluteEncoderReference` abstraction: takes an absolute source + a motor sensor, exposes `angle()`, `isConnected()`, `isConsistent()`, and does the guarded re-seed automatically. The non-blocking `pivotMotor.setPosition(x, 0)` detail (the default overload BLOCKS the main loop up to 100 ms waiting for a CAN ack) is a serious footgun the author had to discover and comment — a library must encode it so nobody rediscovers it.

painPoints.problem: Swerve.java is 500 lines of correctness-critical code copy-pasted between two robots with a 3-line diff — and that diff is entirely inside a comment.
painPoints.evidence: `diff --strip-trailing-cr A/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/Swerve.java B/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/Swerve.java` → 3 lines, all in the `createAprilTagTrackingCommand` Javadoc ('the tag's class, the superstructure's goal, and the selected reef branch side' vs 'the tag's class'). Every SysId routine, the AutoBuilder try/catch, the sim Notifier, the operator-perspective logic, and the FPGA→Phoenix conversion exist twice on disk.
painPoints.libraryFix: PumpkinLib owns `PumpkinSwerve` (extends the Tuner-generated drivetrain, implements Subsystem). Robot repos keep only TunerConstants.java (their real per-robot hardware) and pass in path-following gains + a vision goal strategy. Any future bugfix to timestamp handling or vision rejection lands in one place instead of N.

painPoints.problem: The same fix must be applied N times, and demonstrably already has drifted.
painPoints.evidence: Concrete drift found: `settings.gradle` says `String frcYear = '2025'` in A but `'2026'` in B, while both `.wpilib/wpilib_preferences.json` say `"projectYear": "2026"`. `Robot.java` has `DriverStation.silenceJoystickConnectionWarning(true)` in A but not B. A's `Dashboard` has 4 WPILib `Alert`s (through-bore, elevator sync, coral feedback, low battery); B has only the low-battery one — the shared vitals monitoring silently diverged. A's TunerConstants drive stator limit is `Amps.of(90)`, B's is `Amps.of(60)`, but B's `deploy/pathplanner/settings.json` declares `"driveCurrentLimit": 100.0`.
painPoints.libraryFix: Move the shared surface (Swerve, Vision, Telemetry, Elastic, Dashboard scaffolding, build/gradle conventions) into a versioned PumpkinLib dependency so 'update once' is literally true, and provide a single source of truth for chassis constants that both the code and a PathPlanner-settings exporter read.

painPoints.problem: There is not one tunable number in either repo — every gain, limit, and setpoint requires a code edit + redeploy to change.
painPoints.evidence: `grep -rn "Preferences|getNumber(|LoggedNetworkNumber|LoggedDashboardNumber|TunableNumber|SmartDashboard.getNumber"` across both `src` trees returns ZERO hits outside LimelightHelpers. Every gain is a `public static final double` (e.g. `ELEVATOR_kP = 0.4`, `CORAL_PIVOT_kP = 40.0`, `TRANSLATION_kP = 5.0` in A vs `10.0` in B). The A README's tuning procedure is prose in a Javadoc: 'TUNE - first power-on procedure: 1. Sanity-check the height reading... 2. Raise kG until the carriage just holds... 3. Command a preset and raise kP'. The tuning loop today is: edit Java → `./gradlew deploy` → retest, or leave the code and tune in REV Hardware Client / Tuner X (where the value then disagrees with the committed constant).
painPoints.libraryFix: A `TunableNumber` (LoggedNetworkNumber-backed, no-op-to-constant when not in tuning mode) is the single highest-value thing PumpkinLib can ship for this team. Pair it with a `GainsGroup` that pushes changed values to the controller on change, so the documented three-step procedures become live dashboard sliders instead of edit-deploy cycles.

painPoints.problem: Gains, IDs, and gearing are untyped `double`/`int` with units only in comments — dimensional errors are invisible to the compiler and one class of them is already commented as a hazard.
painPoints.evidence: A/Constants.java carries the convention 'Every value carries its unit in the comment (inches, degrees, amps, ...)', but the values are bare doubles. The degree↔rotation conversion is then done by hand at every Phoenix call site with a literal `/ 360.0`: `config.MotionMagic.MotionMagicCruiseVelocity = CORAL_PIVOT_MAX_VELOCITY / 360.0;`, `config.SoftwareLimitSwitch.ForwardSoftLimitThreshold = CORAL_PIVOT_MAX_ANGLE / 360.0;`, `pivotMotor.setControl(positionRequest.withPosition(targetAngle / 360.0))`, `getMotorAngle() { return pivotMotor.getPosition().getValueAsDouble() * 360.0; }` — nine separate hand-written `/360` or `*360` in CorAl.java alone. CorAl.java even needs a warning comment: '(Phoenix divides rotor rotations by this ratio; do NOT put a rotations-to-degrees multiplier here.)'
painPoints.libraryFix: Use `edu.wpi.first.units` types (`Angle`, `Distance`, `LinearVelocity`) in PumpkinLib's public API — the author already uses them comfortably in TunerConstants (`Amps.of(120.0)`, `Inches.of(2)`, `MetersPerSecond.of(5.96)`). A `MechanismAngle` wrapper that owns the rotations↔degrees boundary would delete every `/360.0` and make the 'do NOT multiply here' comment unnecessary.

painPoints.problem: CAN ID maps and pin maps are maintained as ASCII-art comments with no compile-time or runtime validation, and this has already caused a robot-code crash.
painPoints.evidence: A/Constants.java header comment is a hand-drawn 'CAN ID MAP' table; the code below it carries `// VERIFY: this was previously documented/configured as 64, but Phoenix device IDs only go up to 62 - constructing a device with ID 64 throws and crashes robot code on boot (caught by RobotContainerTest).` The A README elevates this to checklist item 6a. The comment map also has a stale entry: '(63 is free - previously reserved for the removed AlLow mechanism)'. Meanwhile B uses CAN id 5 for a KitBot Spark MAX while A uses CAN id 5 for the CANdle — the same number, different meaning, tracked only in prose.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `CanId` value type with range validation (Phoenix 0-62, REV 1-62) that fails fast with a readable message at construction, plus a `DeviceRegistry` that detects duplicate-ID registration within a robot and can emit the CAN map as a logged artifact instead of a comment that rots.

painPoints.problem: Constants.java is a single monolithic file mixing per-robot hardware IDs, physical geometry, tuning gains, field-layout knowledge, and logging array indices — and the field knowledge is duplicated across robots.
painPoints.evidence: A/Constants.java is 448 lines containing ElevatorConstants, CorAlConstants, SuperstructureConstants, LEDConstants, AutoConstants, VisionConstants (incl. nested TrackingGains), and LoggingConstants. The 2025 Reefscape field tag IDs `REEF_TAGS = {6,7,8,9,10,11,17,18,19,20,21,22}` and `CORAL_STATION_TAGS = {1,2,12,13}` are declared identically in BOTH repos (A lines 405-406, B lines 191-192), as are `REEF_FLUSH_DISTANCE = 0.45`, `STATION_FLUSH_DISTANCE = 0.45`, and the entire `TrackingGains` block (DISTANCE_kP 1.5, ROTATION_kP 0.06, deadbands 0.05/1.0, clamps 2.0/1.0).
painPoints.libraryFix: Separate the axes: PumpkinLib owns field/game constants (tag classes, field dimensions) and default tracking gains; the robot repo owns only its hardware IDs and mechanism geometry. `LoggingConstants` (array index → component) should be replaced by a typed component-pose builder so index/CAD-order mismatch is impossible — currently it's three ints that must match a glTF export order documented in a separate README.

painPoints.problem: Tag-class membership is tested with hand-written linear scans over int arrays, duplicated per tag class per repo.
painPoints.evidence: A/Vision.java lines 131-147 and the identical block in B/Vision.java: `private static boolean isReefTag(int tagId) { for (int tag : VisionConstants.REEF_TAGS) { if (tag == tagId) return true; } return false; }` and the same again for `isCoralStationTag`. Four copies of the same loop across the two repos, running inside `findBestTarget()` on every camera on every 20 ms loop.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `TagClass` enum / `Set<Integer>` lookup in PumpkinLib's field model: `FieldTags.classOf(id)` returning REEF / CORAL_STATION / BARGE / PROCESSOR / UNKNOWN. Deletes four methods and makes 'which tags are trackable' a declarative table.

painPoints.problem: Manual velocity/output clamping is open-coded with nested Math.min/Math.max everywhere instead of a clamp helper.
painPoints.evidence: A/Swerve.java lines 412-414: `vx = Math.min(Math.max(vx, -MAX_LINEAR_VELOCITY), MAX_LINEAR_VELOCITY);` repeated three times in a row (duplicated identically in B/Swerve.java). Also A/Elevator.java:172 `targetPosition = Math.min(Math.max(targetPosition, MIN), MAX)`, A/Elevator.java:210, A/CorAl.java:191, B/AlLow.java:184, B/AlLow.java:213. Java 17 has no `Math.clamp` (added in 21), so every site re-nests.
painPoints.libraryFix: `PumpkinMath.clamp(value, min, max)` and `deadband(value, band)` — trivial, but it removes ~10 error-prone nested expressions and gives one place to add logging/alerting when a command is being clamped (useful during tuning).

painPoints.problem: The elevator's manual control silently multiplies the stick by the speed limit AFTER deadbanding, and the deadband is applied in two different places for the same subsystem.
painPoints.evidence: A/RobotContainer.java lines 297-304 applies `ElevatorConstants.ELEVATOR_MANUAL_CONTROL_DEADBAND` in the default command, and then `Elevator.manualControl` (lines 207-210) applies the SAME deadband again plus the speed limit. CorAl and AlLow put the deadband only inside the subsystem — so the same team has two different conventions for the same concept across three mechanisms in two repos.
painPoints.libraryFix: A single `ManualControl` helper (deadband + scale + optional rate limit) owned by the library and applied in exactly one place, so 'where does the deadband live' stops being a per-mechanism decision.

painPoints.problem: Dead / vestigial logged state that will confuse anyone reading a log.
painPoints.evidence: A/RobotContainer.java lines 123-126 declares `@AutoLogOutput(key = "Draggables/DesiredComponents3d") public static Pose3d[] desiredComponents3d = {new Pose3d(), new Pose3d(), new Pose3d(), new Pose3d()};` — FOUR poses, never written anywhere, while the real `componentPoses` array in Dashboard has THREE. `@AutoLogOutput(key = "Draggables/FreshCode") public static boolean freshCode = true` is flipped once in `disabledExit()` with the comment `// The code isn't fresh anymore! - flaco`. Additionally `Dashboard.componentPoses` is BOTH `@AutoLogOutput(key="Draggables/Components3d")` and explicitly `Logger.recordOutput("RobotState/ComponentPoses", ...)` — the same array logged twice under two keys, and the advantageScopeAssets README references the `Draggables/` key while the main README references the `RobotState/` one.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `ComponentPoses` builder in PumpkinLib that owns the array, its length, its single log key, and the AdvantageScope config contract — so the number of components, the publish order, and the key can't disagree across three files (Constants.LoggingConstants, Dashboard, advantageScopeAssets/Robot_Leviathan/config.json).

painPoints.problem: Formatting is inconsistent within a single repo: tabs and 4-space indentation are mixed file-by-file, and the same file uses different indentation in the two repos.
painPoints.evidence: In A: Constants.java (354 tab-indented lines), TunerConstants.java (249 tabs), Robot.java (92 tabs), Swerve.java (401 tabs), Telemetry.java (92 tabs), Main.java (4 tabs) — but Dashboard.java (241 space lines), RobotContainer.java (253), CorAl.java (327), Elevator.java (209), LEDs.java (136), Vision.java (286), Superstructure.java (356) are all 4-space. TunerConstants.java is tab-indented in A and space-indented in B, which is why a naive diff reported 573 changed lines for a file with only ~15 real differences.
painPoints.libraryFix: Not a library API problem, but PumpkinLib should ship a formatter config (spotless/google-java-format or an .editorconfig) as part of the project template, so cross-robot diffs show real changes only. This directly reduces the cost of the copy-paste-between-robots workflow the team actually uses.

painPoints.problem: Committed simulation/dashboard scratch files and a stale generator project pollute the repos and actively mislead.
painPoints.evidence: A has `networktables.json`, `simgui.json`, `simgui-window.json`, `simgui-ds.json` committed at the repo root (B has only `simgui-ds.json`). `tuner-project.json` (Tuner X project) is committed in both and is documented as WRONG: A/TunerConstants.java header says 'NOTE: tuner-project.json (Tuner X project in the repo root) is STALE - it models all four modules as MK4n (18.75 steer) and holds different CANcoder offsets', and it does — tuner-project.json has FL EncoderOffset -0.07958984375 vs TunerConstants' -0.0888671875. The A README makes 'do not blindly regenerate TunerConstants from it' checklist item #1.
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship a project template with a correct `.gitignore` (sim GUI state, build artifacts) and either exclude the Tuner project or provide a checked verification (a unit test asserting TunerConstants offsets match tuner-project.json, failing loudly when they drift) so a stale generator input can't silently produce a wrong regeneration.

painPoints.problem: Chassis characterization numbers are duplicated between Java and PathPlanner JSON with no cross-check, and are already inconsistent.
painPoints.evidence: B/TunerConstants.java line 82: `kSpeedAt12Volts = MetersPerSecond.of(5.96)` and stator limit `Amps.of(60)`. B/src/main/deploy/pathplanner/settings.json: `"maxDriveSpeed": 5.364`, `"driveCurrentLimit": 100.0`. A is self-consistent (5.96 / 90 in both), B is not — PathPlanner will plan trajectories against a top speed the code doesn't believe in. Both files also independently declare module positions (±0.314 m in JSON, `Inches.of(12.375)` = 0.3143 m in Java), wheel radius, gearing, and mass.
painPoints.libraryFix: One `ChassisConfig` in PumpkinLib as the source of truth, with a gradle task or unit test that validates `deploy/pathplanner/settings.json` against it. This is a silent-failure class of bug (auto just finishes off-target) that a library check catches for free.

painPoints.problem: Roller-stop safety is hand-applied per command instead of guaranteed by construction, and A's coral intake needed an explicit workaround for a rising-edge-only auto-stop.
painPoints.evidence: A/Superstructure.java has `.handleInterrupt(coral::stopIntake)` manually appended to `intakeCoral()`, `ejectCoral()`, and `scoreAlgae()` — with the comment `// Never leave rollers running on interrupt` repeated three times. `intakeCoral()` additionally needs an explicit `Commands.runOnce(coral::stopIntake, coral)` with a 5-line comment explaining that CorAl's periodic auto-stop only fires on the RISING edge, so a piece already latched before the rollers start would leave them running forever. Contrast B/KitBot.java, where `startEnd(..., motor::stopMotor)` makes this structurally impossible.
painPoints.libraryFix: PumpkinLib's `RollerSubsystem` should only expose command factories with stop-on-end built in (the KitBot shape), and a `GamePieceDetector` abstraction should expose a level signal (`isHeld()`) rather than only an edge, so 'run until held' works regardless of prior state.

painPoints.problem: Vision goal resolution — the one genuinely robot-specific part of Vision — is entangled with the copy-pasted 200 lines around it, forcing a full-file fork.
painPoints.evidence: The Vision.java diff between A and B is 99 lines, and every one of them is in the goal-resolver area: A has `BranchSide`, `setGoalSupplier(Supplier<Superstructure.Goal>)`, `tagMatchesCurrentGoal(int)` and a 13-line switch over `Superstructure.Goal`; B collapses all of it to `return Optional.of(new TrackingGoal(0.0, REEF_FLUSH_DISTANCE));` and filters with `if (getTrackingGoal(tagId).isEmpty()) continue;`. The other ~205 lines (MegaTag fusion, camera table name precomputation, `AprilTagTarget`, `toggleTracking`, caching) are identical.
painPoints.libraryFix: Make the goal resolver a first-class interface: `interface TrackingGoalResolver { Optional<TrackingGoal> resolve(int tagId); }`. Then B is a two-line lambda, A supplies its superstructure-aware implementation, and 205 lines of fusion/caching live in PumpkinLib. This is the cleanest seam in the entire survey.

constraints: Java 17 only — both repos pin `sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility = JavaVersion.VERSION_17`. No `Math.clamp` (Java 21), no records-in-patterns, no sealed-interface pattern matching. PumpkinLib must compile and run on 17.

Must work with GradleRIO 2026.2.1 / WPILib 2026 and the exact vendordep set already in use: Phoenix6 26.3.0, REVLib 2026.0.5, PathplannerLib 2026.1.2, AdvantageKit 26.0.2. Note GradleRIO 2026 hard-rejects vendordeps with a mismatched `frcYear` (this is why ChoreoLib is deliberately absent — documented in both READMEs).

Must not fight CTRE's Tuner-X-generated `TunerConstants.java` format. That file is regenerated by an external tool; PumpkinLib has to consume `SwerveDrivetrainConstants` + `SwerveModuleConstants<?,?,?>...` and extend `SwerveDrivetrain<TalonFX, TalonFX, CANcoder>` rather than replace it. The team already hand-edits it (per-module steer ratios for mixed MK4i/MK4n) so the library must tolerate hand-edited generated files.

Mixed-vendor hardware is mandatory, not optional: CTRE TalonFX/Kraken (swerve, A's CorAl) AND REV Spark MAX/NEO (A's elevator, B's KitBot + AlLow) in the same robot. Any motor abstraction must cover both, including their very different closed-loop idioms (Phoenix `MotionMagicVoltage` + `SensorToMechanismRatio` vs REVLib `kMAXMotionPositionControl` + `positionConversionFactor` + on-controller `FeedForwardConfig`).

Closed-loop control runs ON the motor controller, not the roboRIO, and the setpoint is expected to LATCH. This is a deliberate, repeatedly documented design choice ('The controller latches the setpoint; no need to re-send every loop'; 'the arm keeps holding its angle no matter which command is currently scheduled'). PumpkinLib must not impose a roboRIO-side periodic control loop that breaks the latch semantics — B's AlLowSimTest exists specifically as a regression net for it ('this was the original hold-position bug').

Motor configuration must persist to flash (`ResetMode.kResetSafeParameters, PersistMode.kPersistParameters` used everywhere) so a brownout can't revert controllers mid-match. Any config abstraction must preserve this.

Must not block the main loop on CAN. Explicitly encoded in A/CorAl.java: `pivotMotor.setPosition(x, 0)` with a zero timeout because 'the default setPosition overload BLOCKS the main loop waiting for the device ack (up to 100 ms)'. Similarly Vision uses `SetRobotOrientation_NoFlush` + one `LimelightHelpers.Flush()` per loop rather than per camera.

Vision timestamps must be converted FPGA→Phoenix (`Utils.fpgaToCurrentTime`) before reaching the CTRE pose estimator — hard requirement, documented as 'Passing raw FPGA time makes every measurement appear to be from the wrong moment and corrupts the pose estimate.'
Field-legal network ports only: 5800-5810. The layout WebServer takes 5800, so AdvantageKit's RLOGServer is pinned to 5810. A library that opens its own port must stay in that window and not collide.

AdvantageKit is used for LOGGING ONLY — no IO layers, no `@AutoLog` inputs classes, no deterministic replay. The A README states this explicitly: 'full AdvantageKit log replay would additionally require IO-layer hardware abstraction in every subsystem — not done here.' PumpkinLib should not force an IO-layer architecture on this team unless it's opt-in; their subsystems own hardware directly.

Dashboard target is Elastic (not Shuffleboard — 'Elastic dropped Shuffleboard API support'). Publishing must be plain NetworkTables under /SmartDashboard plus a `deploy/elastic-layout.json`, and the vendored `util/Elastic.java` (Gold87 ElasticLib) helper must keep working for `selectTab` and toast notifications.

Unit tests construct real (simulated) CAN devices, and vendor libs reject duplicate device IDs within one JVM — hence `forkEvery = 1` in build.gradle. Any library test utilities must survive that constraint.

Desktop simulation must keep working (`includeDesktopSupport = true`, `wpi.sim.addGui().defaultEnabled = true`). Known caveat to preserve/route around: REV's simulated MAXMotion advances on wall-clock time and mis-scales feedforward, which is why ElevatorSimTest deliberately does NOT assert a full profile move.

Gradle is pinned to the WPILib JDK via `org.gradle.java.home=C:/Users/Public/wpilib/2026/jdk` because the machine's JAVA_HOME (Android Studio JBR) ships an msvcp140.dll that hard-crashes WPILib natives. Any build-template PumpkinLib ships must keep or document this escape hatch.

Team 9143 runs multiple robots simultaneously off one codebase lineage (A competition robot + B KitBot/practice robot). PumpkinLib must support per-robot divergence cleanly — different mechanisms, different auto gains (A: translation/rotation kP 5.0/5.0; B: 10.0/7.0), different CANcoder offsets, and a robot with ZERO cameras where the whole vision stack must stay inert without crashing (B guards its Y-binding with `if (VisionConstants.LIMELIGHT_NAMES.length > 0)`).

summary: 18 Java files / ~3,080 LOC of a real, working, competition-season robot: swerve + 4-camera PhotonVision fusion + a 3-DOF shoot-on-the-move turret/rack/flywheel + ground intake + CANdle LEDs, driven by PathPlanner autos. It is genuinely team-authored (only TunerConstants.java is CTRE-generated), and the shooter math is the most sophisticated thing in the survey set: an iterative virtual-target solver compensating for robot translation, robot rotation crossed with the off-center turret offset, and indexer-imparted ball spin. Architecture is plain WPILib command-based with NO AdvantageKit, no IO layers, no simulation beyond CTRE's generated swerve sim thread, and no test sources at all. Everything is tuned by editing Constants.java (or a `static {}` block of InterpolatingDoubleTreeMaps inside ShooterSubsystem) and redeploying — SmartDashboard is used write-only, with zero getNumber/Preferences/tunable-number reads anywhere. The dominant cost centers are: five near-identical Command classes that copy-paste the same alliance-target-selection block; hand-rolled per-motor Slot0Configs/CurrentLimits/soft-limit boilerplate repeated in every subsystem; ad-hoc `degrees ÷ 360 ÷ negativeGearRatio` conversions with sign hacks; and three disagreeing sources of truth for drivetrain geometry (tuner-project.json vs TunerConstants.java vs pathplanner/settings.json). CLAUDE.md is well-written but already stale — it documents files, bindings, and versions that no longer exist.
stack: Java 17 (`sourceCompatibility = VERSION_17`, build.gradle:6-9). GradleRIO 2026.2.1. Vendordeps: Phoenix6 26.1.1, PathplannerLib 2026.1.2, photonlib v2026.2.2, WPILibNewCommands 1.0.0 (CLAUDE.md claims Phoenix 26.1.0 and PhotonVision v2026.1.1 — both stale). Hardware: 4x SDS L3 swerve modules with WCP Kraken X60 TalonFX drive+steer, CANcoders (RemoteCANcoder feedback, not FusedCANcoder — "requires Phoenix Pro"), Pigeon 2 (ID 5), all on the "rio" bus; 5 more TalonFX on the intake (IDs 20-24), 3 on the shooter/turret (25-27), 1 turret indexer (28), 1 CTRE CANdle (29) driving 7 onboard + 60 strip LEDs. 4x PhotonVision cameras (Back_Left/Back_Right/Front_Left/Front_Right). Autos: PathPlanner AutoBuilder + NamedCommands + SendableChooser, 6 autos / 20 paths in src/main/deploy/pathplanner. Logging/replay: CTRE SignalLogger (hoot) + `HootAutoReplay().withTimestampReplay().withJoystickReplay()` (Robot.java:19-21). No AdvantageKit, no Choreo. `includeDesktopSupport = true`, `wpi.sim.addGui().defaultEnabled = true`, JUnit 5 wired in build.gradle:74-81 but `src/test` does not exist.

patterns.name: Multi-camera AprilTag fusion with validation + distance-scaled std devs
patterns.whatItDoes: Bundles each PhotonCamera with its PhotonPoseEstimator, robotToCamera Transform3d and a name into a private `CameraConfig` class; iterates all of them, drains `getAllUnreadResults()` but only processes the newest frame (explicitly to avoid an overrun feedback spiral), prefers `estimateCoprocMultiTagPose` and falls back to `estimateLowestAmbiguityPose`, rejects estimates using blacklisted tag IDs, rejects ambiguity > 0.2 on single-tag, rejects poses outside field bounds +/-0.5 m, rejects avg tag distance > 6 m, then scales base std devs by `1.0 + d^2/30.0`. Results come back as a record and are pushed into the drivetrain from a default command.

patterns.name: Shoot-on-the-move iterative virtual-target solver
patterns.whatItDoes: Fixed-point iteration (10 passes) walking the aim point backwards along projected drift during flight. Correctly derives the *launch point's* field velocity rather than chassis velocity, adding the tangential term from robot angular rate crossed with the turret's off-center offset. Then adds indexer-spin correction decomposed into along-barrel (cos(turretAngle)) and perpendicular (sin(turretAngle)) components, both multiplied by flight time from an empirical distance->seconds table.

patterns.libraryValue: Every shooter game re-derives this and most teams get the omega-cross-r term wrong. A `MotionCompensatedAimSolver` — inputs (target Translation3d, launch pose, field-relative ChassisSpeeds, flight-time lookup), outputs (virtual target, converged flag, iterations used) — is directly liftable. The library version should add what is missing here: a convergence tolerance instead of a hardcoded 10 iterations, and a divergence guard so it cannot sit in a limit cycle.

patterns.name: Continuous-turret angle unwrapping with soft-limit wraparound
patterns.whatItDoes: Converts a desired absolute turret angle into a motor position while tracking the last commanded angle, so the turret follows smoothly across the +/-180 degree atan2 discontinuity instead of unwinding. If the unwrapped target would exceed a physical limit it wraps 360 degrees to the other side of the >360-degree travel range, then safety-clamps. Paired with soft limits derived from the same degree constants at class-init.

painPoints.problem: Three disagreeing sources of truth for the same drivetrain geometry

TunerConstants.java:92-96 says `kCoupleRatio = 5.4`, `kDriveGearRatio = 5.67`, `kSteerGearRatio = 12.1`; TunerConstants.java:143 says `kFrontLeftEncoderOffset = Rotations.of(0.15717)`; module positions are `Inches.of(10)` (a 20 in track, not 22.5 in). src/main/deploy/pathplanner/settings.json independently repeats `driveGearing: 5.67`, `robotTrackwidth: 0.508`, `flModuleX: 0.254`, `maxDriveSpeed: 5.44`. painPoints.problem: Encoder seeding double-applies the gear ratio (latent bug, currently masked by a zero value)

painPoints.problem: Gear ratios encode direction as a negative number and are divided rather than multiplied, with a comment admitting the confusion

Also: load the shot tables from `Filesystem.getDeployDirectory()` so they can be re-tuned between matches without a rebuild.

painPoints.problem: `optimizeBusUtilization()` is called on motors whose status signals are never re-enabled — a silent stale-data trap
painPoints.evidence: ShooterSubsystem.java:180, :185, :189 call `optimizeBusUtilization()` on all three shooter motors with no preceding `setUpdateFrequency`. GroundIntakeSubsystem.java:92-93 shows the author knows the correct pattern (`m_leftPivotMotor.getPosition().setUpdateFrequency(50); m_leftPivotMotor.optimizeBusUtilization();`) but it is applied in only one of eight call sites. Any future `getPosition()`/`getVelocity()` read on a shooter motor returns a frozen value with no error — and `isAtPosition`-style logic built on it would silently never be true.
painPoints.libraryFix: A motor-configuration builder where you declare which signals you consume, and it derives the `setUpdateFrequency` calls and the `optimizeBusUtilization()` call in the correct order — making it impossible to optimize away a signal you asked for.

painPoints.problem: Camera count is hardcoded into method signatures across three files, with a transposable all-boolean argument list
painPoints.evidence: VisionSubsystem has four camera fields, four estimators and four `isBackLeftConnected()`-style methods (:347-376); `Telemetry.updateVision(List, boolean, boolean, boolean, boolean)` (:165) takes one boolean per camera plus four dedicated BooleanPublisher fields (:69-72); RobotContainer.java:193 passes them as `(estimates, vision.isBackLeftConnected(), vision.isBackRightConnected(), vision.isFrontRightConnected(), vision.isFrontLeftConnected())` — four same-typed positional booleans that would swap silently.

painPoints.problem: Zero simulation support for anything the team wrote — the highest-risk math is untestable off-robot
painPoints.evidence: The only sim is CTRE-generated: `startSimThread()` with a 4 ms Notifier calling `updateSimState` (CommandSwerveDrivetrain.java:41-42, :292-305). `Robot.simulationPeriodic()` is empty (Robot.java:82). Grep for `isSimulation|Sim(` outside CommandSwerveDrivetrain returns nothing — no TalonFXSimState for intake/turret/rack/flywheel, no VisionSystemSim/PhotonCameraSim, no SingleJointedArmSim/FlywheelSim. `src/test` does not exist at all. So the shoot-on-the-move solver, the turret unwrapping, the shot tables and the pivot seeding can only be validated on a real robot during a real match.
painPoints.libraryFix: Library-side simulated mechanism wrappers (arm/elevator/flywheel/turret backed by WPILib physics sims and auto-wired to TalonFXSimState) that activate on `RobotBase.isSimulation()` with no team code changes, plus a PhotonVision VisionSystemSim built from the same `CameraSpec` list used on the real robot. Keeping the pure math (aim solver, angle unwrap, gearing conversion, shot tables) HAL-free so it is unit-testable is the single highest-leverage design constraint for PumpkinLib.

painPoints.problem: `getEstimatedPoses()` returns a shared mutable buffer
painPoints.evidence: VisionSubsystem.java:58 `private final List<VisionPoseEstimate> m_estimatesBuffer = new ArrayList<>(4);` and :155-163 `m_estimatesBuffer.clear(); ...; return m_estimatesBuffer;`. RobotContainer.java:181-193 holds that list, iterates it, then hands the same reference to `logger.updateVision(estimates, ...)`. It works today only because both consumers run before the next call; any caller that retains the list gets it silently emptied 20 ms later.
painPoints.libraryFix: Push-based API (`vision.consumeEstimates(drivetrain::addVisionMeasurement)` or a registered consumer) instead of returning a recycled collection — keeps the zero-allocation benefit without exposing the aliasing hazard.

painPoints.problem: Documentation and repo hygiene drift

CLAUDE.md:15-17 documents `./gradlew test` and .vscode/settings.json defines a `WPIlibUnitTests` config, but `src/test` does not exist. A 12.7 MB GIF named `Right Side Auto` is committed at the repo root. TunerConstants.java:84 still has the generator default `new CANBus("", "./logs/example.hoot")`.
painPoints.libraryFix: Out of scope for the library core, but PumpkinLib should ship a project template/archetype with constants layout, a smoke-test source set, and a task that generates the structure/bindings documentation from the code so it cannot drift by hand.

constraints: Java 17 exactly — build.gradle:6-9 pins sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility to VERSION_17. No language features beyond 17 (records and sealed types are fine; pattern-matching switch is not).

GradleRIO 2026.2.1 with WPILib 2026 and vendordep-based resolution (build.gradle:1-3; settings.gradle resolves the frcHome maven under C:/Users/Public/wpilib/2026). PumpkinLib must ship as a vendordep JSON (or a composite/source dependency) resolvable by GradleRIO 2026, and must survive the fat-jar packaging in build.gradle:90-95.

CTRE Phoenix 6 v26.1.1 is the entire hardware layer — TalonFX, CANcoder, Pigeon 2, CANdle, Slot0Configs, MotionMagicVoltage, PositionVoltage, VelocityVoltage, Follower, NeutralOut, StaticBrake, SolidColor/RGBWColor. There is not a single REV/SparkMax device in the repo. Any hardware abstraction must be zero-cost for a pure-CTRE team and must not hide Phoenix's on-motor closed loop behind a roboRIO-side controller.

CTRE Tuner X owns src/main/java/frc/robot/generated/TunerConstants.java and can regenerate it at any time (CLAUDE.md:87: 'avoid manual edits unless updating specific values'). tuner-project.json at the repo root is likewise Tuner X's file. The library must consume TunerConstants, never require edits inside it.

The swerve drivetrain is inheritance-bound: `CommandSwerveDrivetrain extends TunerSwerveDrivetrain implements Subsystem` where `TunerSwerveDrivetrain extends SwerveDrivetrain<TalonFX,TalonFX,CANcoder>` (TunerConstants.java:219). A library drivetrain abstraction cannot supply its own base class — it must work by composition, by interface, or via the same subclass hook, and must preserve the CTRE idioms already in use: `registerTelemetry(Consumer<SwerveDriveState>)` and `applyRequest(Supplier<SwerveRequest>)`.

Vision timestamps must be translated between FPGA time and Phoenix time. CommandSwerveDrivetrain.java:314-350 overrides all three `addVisionMeasurement`/`samplePoseAt` entry points solely to wrap timestamps in `Utils.fpgaToCurrentTime(...)`. Any library vision path feeding a CTRE pose estimator must do the same or it silently corrupts the Kalman fusion.

PathPlanner 2026.1.2 is the auto framework and its call ordering is load-bearing: `NamedCommands.registerCommand(...)` must run BEFORE `AutoBuilder.configure(...)` (RobotContainer.java:70-76 has an explicit comment about this), `RobotConfig.fromGUISettings()` reads src/main/deploy/pathplanner/settings.json, `AutoBuilder.buildAutoChooser()` populates the SendableChooser, and the drive consumer must forward `feedforwards.robotRelativeForcesXNewtons()/Y` into `SwerveRequest.ApplyRobotSpeeds` (CommandSwerveDrivetrain.java:208-236).

Logging is CTRE SignalLogger/hoot, not AdvantageKit. `SignalLogger.start()` is called from the Telemetry constructor (Telemetry.java:41) and `HootAutoReplay().withTimestampReplay().withJoystickReplay()` is updated first thing in robotPeriodic (Robot.java:19-21, :29). Do not design the library around AdvantageKit's Logger/IO-layer/@AutoLog model or around a Robot base class that owns the logging lifecycle — it must coexist with hoot replay and with registerTelemetry.

`optimizeBusUtilization()` is applied to every TalonFX in the project (8 call sites). Any library code that reads status signals must explicitly `setUpdateFrequency` on the signals it needs first, or loudly document that it does not — otherwise it will read frozen values on this robot.

Stated team conventions (CLAUDE.md:61-66): `m_fieldName` private fields, `kConstantName` or UPPER_SNAKE_CASE constants, packages under `frc.robot.{subsystems, constants, commands, generated}`, and 'Use WPILib Units system for type-safe measurements'. In practice the units guidance is honored only in generated TunerConstants and RobotContainer's `.in(MetersPerSecond)`; team code is raw doubles with units baked into constant names (`_METERS`, `_ROTATIONS`, `_RPS2`, `_DEG`, `_MS`). A units-typed library API matches the stated convention but is a migration for existing code, so it needs raw-double escape hatches.

Subsystem base-class choice is inconsistent and must be tolerated: hand-written mechanisms use `implements Subsystem` (ShooterSubsystem, TurretSubsystem, GroundIntakeSubsystem, CommandSwerveDrivetrain) while VisionSubsystem and LEDSubsystem `extends SubsystemBase`. Any library base class must be optional, not mandatory.

No test infrastructure exists (`src/test` absent) despite JUnit 5 wired in build.gradle:74-81 and a WPIlibUnitTests launch config in .vscode/settings.json. The library must be useful with zero tests written, but should keep its pure-math surface (aim solver, angle unwrapping, gearing conversion, shot tables, deadband) HAL-free so it can be exercised off-robot.

Windows-only dev environment: JAVA_HOME is C:/Users/Public/wpilib/2026/jdk per .claude/settings.local.json, and .vscode/settings.json uses ${workspaceFolder}/build/jni/release. Any build scripts or codegen the library ships must work on Windows and under Git Bash.

Confirmed via .git/config remote `https://github.com/patribots4738/reefscape2025`, `.wpilib/wpilib_preferences.json` teamNumber 4738, and README ("The Patribots (FRC 4738)", patribots.org). NOT a fork — this is the team's own upstream repo, cloned. 19 contributors (top: PatribotsProgramming 278 commits, Oliver-Cushman 153, Eva Klekowski 45); last commit 2025-11-29. Student-written and student-maintained, publicly open-sourced, competition-proven (commit 2d5b875 "We f***ing won"). 68 Java files / 13,935 lines team-authored, of which LimelightHelpers.java (1,644 lines) is vendored from LimelightLib.
summary: This is a mature, genuinely well-architected AdvantageKit repo and the single best reference design in the survey set — but it is also a monument to hand-rolled infrastructure that a library should absorb. The architecture is textbook 6328-influenced: `LoggedRobot`, strict `XxxIO` interface + `@AutoLog XxxIOInputs` + `XxxIOKraken`/`XxxIONeo` triads for every mechanism, subsystems holding `io` + `inputsAutoLogged`, and a non-Subsystem `Superstructure` coordinator that composes Commands over five child subsystems via a `SuperState`/`ArmState`/`ClimbState`/`ClawState` state machine with explicit collision-avoidance sequencing (`fixArmAndClimb`, `avoidClimb`, `transitionWrist`). The crown jewel is `Kraken extends TalonFX` (1,227 lines) — a full vendor wrapper with a unit-conversion factor, a `ControlPreference` enum selecting among 12 pre-allocated CTRE request objects, a `TelemetryPreference` enum that drives per-signal update frequencies, retry-until-verified config application via `DeviceUtil.applyParameter`, three gain slots, and built-in `DCMotorSim` ticking; `SafeSpark`/`Neo` (1,256 lines combined) is the REV twin. All configuration lives in a single 1,253-line `Constants.java` holding ~20 nested `public static final class` blocks, with gains expressed as a hand-rolled `GainConstants` POJO. Tuning is entirely compile-time: a complete `LoggedTunableNumber`/`LoggedGainConstants` tunable stack was built and then deliberately commented out everywhere (30+ commented declarations across 9 files) for competition lockdown, leaving no runtime tuning path at all. The most valuable extraction targets are the Kraken/SafeSpark wrappers, the retry-verify config primitive, the IO-triad shape, and the state machine; the most valuable *warnings* are two live positional-overload bugs in `GainConstants`/`Kraken.setGains` that silently mis-assign feedforward terms, plus ~500 lines of dead abstractions (`LoggedSuperState`, `OICalc`, `Scale3d`, all five `*IONeo` classes, `MAXSwerveModuleConstants`).

Vendordeps: AdvantageKit 4.1.2 (+ akit-autolog annotationProcessor wired in build.gradle from the vendordep JSON version), PathplannerLib 2025.2.7, CTRE Phoenix6 25.4.0, REVLib 2025.0.3, WPILibNewCommands 1.0.0. Also `gov.nist.math:jama:1.0.3` (for PolynomialRegression), JUnit Jupiter 5.10.1, `com.peterabeles.gversion` 1.10.3 generating `frc/robot/BuildConstants.java`. Hardware: Kraken X60 FOC on MK4c swerve (L2, 5.9:1) with CANcoder per module (CAN 21-24) and Pigeon2 (CAN 29) on a separate "Drivebase" CAN bus; Kraken elevator (2x, leader/follower, 9:1), Kraken wrist (60:1 + DutyCycleEncoder on DIO 7), Kraken climb (422.4:1), Kraken coral claw + algae claw; 2x Limelight ("limelight-four" + "limelight-threeg") via vendored LimelightHelpers; REV PDH at CAN 30. A complete parallel REV/NEO + MAXSwerve hardware path exists but is entirely unreferenced from live code. patterns.name: Kraken — full TalonFX wrapper with unit conversion, control-mode preference, and telemetry preference
patterns.whatItDoes: Extends TalonFX to give every motor: (1) a `unitConversionFactor` so callers speak meters/radians instead of rotations — every setter divides by it and every getter multiplies by it; (2) a `ControlPreference` enum {VOLTAGE, TORQUE_CURRENT, MM_VOLTAGE, MM_TORQUE_CURRENT} that selects among 12 pre-allocated CTRE request objects so `setTargetPosition(double)` works identically regardless of control mode; (3) a `TelemetryPreference` enum {DEFAULT, NO_ENCODER, SWERVE} that sets per-signal CAN update frequencies (fast/mid/slow) and a matching `refreshSignals()` that only refreshes the signals that preference actually uses; (4) three gain slots with per-term setters; (5) `register()` into a static map plus a `tick()` DCMotorSim step.
patterns.whereSeen: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/reefscape2025/src/main/java/frc/robot/util/hardware/phoenix/Kraken.java (1227 lines). Consumed by ElevatorIOKraken, WristIOKraken, ClimbIOKraken, CoralClawIOKraken, AlgaeClawIOKraken, ModuleIOKraken. REV twin: util/hardware/rev/SafeSpark.java (842) + Neo.java (414). Siblings: CANCoderCustom.java (215), Pigeon2Custom.java (241).
patterns.libraryValue: This is the highest-value extraction in the entire survey. The unit-conversion-factor idea alone eliminates the single most common FRC bug class (rotations vs. mechanism units). The TelemetryPreference→signal-frequency coupling is a CAN-bus-utilization optimization most teams never do and cannot easily discover. PumpkinLib should ship this as a first-class `PumpkinTalonFX`/`PumpkinSparkMax` pair behind ONE shared interface so IO impls become vendor-agnostic — note the team wrote the Kraken and Neo wrappers with near-identical method surfaces (`setGains` vs `setPID`, `setPercentOutput` vs `set`) but no common interface, which is exactly why they need five dead `*IONeo` classes to switch vendors.

patterns.name: DeviceUtil.applyParameter — retry-until-verified hardware configuration
patterns.whatItDoes: Every single config call (inversion, current limits, soft limits, gains, gear ratio, brake mode, Motion Magic, signal frequency) goes through a primitive that takes an apply-supplier, a refresh-supplier, and a boolean parameter-check, then loops up to MAX_ATTEMPTS (4 normally, 20 in 'safe hardware mode'), re-reading the value back off the device and verifying it actually took. It logs which attempt succeeded, and short-circuits entirely in simulation.
patterns.whereSeen: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/reefscape2025/src/main/java/frc/robot/util/hardware/phoenix/DeviceUtil.java (74 lines); every config method in Kraken.java calls it, e.g. Kraken.java:520-531 (setSupplyCurrentLimit), :580-594 (setSoftLimits), :922-945 (applyGains).
patterns.libraryValue: This directly addresses the #1 cause of 'the robot worked yesterday' — a CAN config silently failing to apply at boot. Almost no team does read-back verification. PumpkinLib should make this the ONLY way to configure hardware, so it is impossible to write an unverified config call. Note the clever XOR verification idiom they use to handle the zero case: `(cfg.StatorCurrentLimit != 0 ^ currentLimit == 0)` — meaning 'nonzero unless we asked for zero'. That idiom is subtle enough that a library should encapsulate it rather than ask users to reproduce it.

patterns.name: The IO triad — interface + @AutoLog inputs struct + per-vendor impl, one per mechanism
patterns.whatItDoes: Every mechanism is exactly three files: `XxxIO` (interface with `@AutoLog class XxxIOInputs` and all-default no-op methods), `XxxIOKraken`, `XxxIONeo`. The subsystem holds `private final XxxIO io;` and `private final XxxIOInputsAutoLogged inputs = new XxxIOInputsAutoLogged();`, and `periodic()` always opens with `io.updateInputs(inputs); Logger.processInputs("SubsystemInputs/Xxx", inputs);`. Default-method interfaces mean a partial impl compiles without stubs. Inputs always carry a `motorConnected` boolean sourced from `refreshSignals().isOK()`.
patterns.whereSeen: Uniformly applied across all seven mechanisms: subsystems/superstructure/elevator/{ElevatorIO,ElevatorIOKraken,ElevatorIONeo}.java, .../wrist/, .../climb/, .../claw/ClawIO.java (shared by both algae and coral claws), subsystems/drive/module/{ModuleIO,ModuleIOKraken,ModuleIONeo}.java, subsystems/drive/gyro/{GyroIO,GyroIOPigeon2}.java, subsystems/vision/{VisionIO,VisionIOLimelight}.java.
patterns.libraryValue: The shape is correct and worth codifying, but the *content* is 90% mechanical. `ElevatorIOKraken.updateInputs` is 14 near-identical assignment lines; `WristIOKraken`, `ClimbIOKraken`, `CoralClawIOKraken` repeat the same 6-7 line block verbatim. PumpkinLib should provide a `MotorInputs` struct plus a `populateFrom(PumpkinMotor)` helper so an IO impl for a single-motor mechanism is ~10 lines instead of ~90, and reuse of one `ClawIO` across two subsystems (as they did for algae/coral) becomes the norm rather than a one-off.

patterns.name: Superstructure state machine — SuperState composed of orthogonal ArmState/ClimbState/ClawState with interrupt suppliers
patterns.whatItDoes: A non-Subsystem coordinator owning five subsystems and a `Set<Subsystem> requirements`. ~50 named `SuperState` fields (STOW, L1..L4, L2_WITH_ALGAE, NET_PREP_FAR, CLIMB_FINAL, ...) each bundling an `ArmState` (elevator meters + wrist radians), a `ClimbState` (position + slam flag), a `ClawState` (coral percent + algae percent), and two `BooleanSupplier` interrupts that let the claw start early rather than waiting for full mechanism arrival. `setSuperState(next)` runs arm/climb choreography in parallel with claw scheduling. Collision avoidance is explicit: `fixArmAndClimb` branches on whether the climb must move and whether the arm goal is safe for the climb, routing through `avoidClimb`/`transitionWrist`. Runtime-derived transitions use `Commands.defer(() -> setSuperState(getPlacementState()), requirements)` with arrow-switch state derivation.
patterns.whereSeen: C:/Users/ericj/GitHub/reefscape2025/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/superstructure/Superstructure.java (727 lines) and SuperState.java (47 lines, six telescoping constructors).
patterns.libraryValue: This is the best-articulated FRC state machine in the survey and the strongest argument that PumpkinLib needs a first-class state-machine module. Two ideas are worth lifting wholesale: (a) composing a state from *orthogonal* per-mechanism sub-states rather than one flat enum, which is what keeps 50 states tractable; (b) the interrupt-supplier escape hatch, which solves the real-world 'don't wait for the elevator to finish before spinning the intake' problem declaratively. The `Commands.defer(..., requirements)` idiom for late-bound state selection is also a subtle correctness win most teams get wrong.

patterns.name: RIO-side trapezoid profile with swappable fast/slow constraint sets
patterns.whatItDoes: Elevator and Wrist each hold two `TrapezoidProfile` objects (fast/slow) and a `shouldRunFast` flag chosen per-call by a `BooleanSupplier`. `periodic()` integrates one 20ms profile step and feeds only the *step* position to the motor's closed loop, rather than handing the motor the final goal. When disabled, the setpoint is continuously re-seeded from measured position so re-enabling never jumps. The fast/slow choice is driven by game state — `shouldRunElevatorFast()` returns false when carrying algae, so the mechanism automatically moves gently when holding a game piece.
patterns.whereSeen: subsystems/superstructure/elevator/Elevator.java:44-45,72-81,103-111 and subsystems/superstructure/wrist/Wrist.java:74-83,94-102 — the two implementations are near-verbatim duplicates. Selection logic: Superstructure.java:627-654.
patterns.libraryValue: The 'profile on the RIO, closed loop on the motor' split plus disabled-state setpoint re-seeding is exactly the pattern a `PumpkinPositionMechanism` base class should provide for free, along with `atPosition(tolerance)`/`atTargetPosition()`. The fast/slow-by-payload idea generalizes to 'constraint profiles selected by a supplier', which is a nice declarative API. Extracting this deletes ~80 duplicated lines between Elevator and Wrist immediately.

patterns.name: LoggedTunableNumber / LoggedGainConstants — Trigger-based hot-reload of gains
patterns.whatItDoes: `LoggedTunableNumber extends LoggedNetworkNumber`, tracking `previousValue` in `periodic()` and exposing `ifChanged()` plus a `Trigger onChanged(Command)` that is hard-gated by `!DriverStation.isFMSAttached()`. `LoggedGainConstants` composes seven of them (P/I/D/A/S/V/G, key-prefixed `0-P`..`6-G` so they sort correctly in dashboards) and ORs their triggers, so one subscription re-pushes a whole gain set to hardware.
patterns.whereSeen: util/custom/LoggedTunableNumber.java (39), LoggedTunableBoolean.java (39), LoggedGainConstants.java (57). Intended wiring survives only as comments, e.g. Elevator.java:60 `// ElevatorConstants.LOGGED_GAINS.onChanged(Commands.runOnce(() -> io.setGains(...)).ignoringDisable(true));`
patterns.libraryValue: The design is right — FMS-gating, `.ignoringDisable(true)`, and Trigger-based push-on-change are all correct choices. But it was commented out wholesale rather than switched off, which is the real lesson: PumpkinLib must make tunables **zero-cost and centrally toggleable** (one `TUNING_MODE` flag that compiles/behaves as a plain constant when false) so teams never face the choice between 'tunable' and 'safe at competition' that drove this team to comment out 30+ declarations by hand.

patterns.name: ActiveConditionalCommand — conditional that re-evaluates while running
patterns.whatItDoes: A WPILib `ConditionalCommand` variant that re-checks its condition every `execute()`; when the condition flips it ends the current branch with interrupted=true and re-initializes into the other branch. Correctly unions both branches' requirements, delegates `runsWhenDisabled`, and computes `getInterruptionBehavior` as the conservative union.
patterns.whereSeen: util/custom/ActiveConditionalCommand.java (100 lines; the class javadoc reads "This class was created by team 4738. It is not part of the official WPILib API."). Used in RobotContainer.java:303,311,399 for driver align-target selection and Superstructure.java:432,442 for high-vs-low algae reef selection.
patterns.libraryValue: Small, correct, genuinely missing from WPILib, and needed by every team that does pose-dependent auto-align or target selection. A near-free win for PumpkinLib's command library. Ship as-is with tests.

patterns.name: PatriBoxController — square-to-circle joystick remap plus rumble-as-Command
patterns.whatItDoes: Extends `CommandXboxController`, overriding `getLeftX/Y` and `getRightX/Y` to route through `toCircle(x,y)`, which maps the Xbox stick's chamfered-square envelope onto a true unit circle via piecewise slope regions (documented with a public Desmos link). Also inverts Y at the source so 'forward is positive', applies deadband before remapping, and exposes `setRumble(DoubleSupplier, double duration)` as a Command that auto-clears — with rumble suppressed outside TELEOP.
patterns.whereSeen: util/custom/PatriBoxController.java (243 lines). Math referenced at README line 73 and https://www.desmos.com/calculator/e07raajzh5.
patterns.libraryValue: Joystick response shaping is something every team wants and nobody gets right; shipping a validated circularization plus deadband-before-shaping ordering is a real differentiator. The rumble-as-auto-clearing-Command with game-mode gating is a small ergonomic gem. Caveat for the library: this file also contains 24 methods marked "will be unnecessary in 2025" that are still present in 2025 code — PumpkinLib should version-gate compatibility shims rather than let them accrete.

patterns.name: LocalADStarAK — deterministic pathfinding under AdvantageKit log replay
patterns.whatItDoes: Wraps PathPlanner's ADStar pathfinder so its inputs/outputs are pushed through the AdvantageKit `Logger`, making pathfinding results identical on replay instead of re-running nondeterministic search.
patterns.whereSeen: util/auto/LocalADStarAK.java (148 lines); installed at Robot.java:64 `Pathfinding.setPathfinder(new LocalADStarAK());`.
patterns.libraryValue: Replay-determinism is the entire value proposition of AdvantageKit, and pathfinding is the most common thing that silently breaks it. PumpkinLib should ship this (upstream-derived) adapter pre-wired so replay correctness is the default, not a thing teams discover after a confusing log session.

patterns.name: Alliance-flipped field constants via mirror/flip + subList windowing
patterns.whatItDoes: Field poses are authored once for blue, then red variants are generated at class-init by `PoseCalculations.flipPose`/`mirrorPose` and appended to the same List. Accessors return an alliance-selected window: `GET_REEF_FACE_POSITIONS()` returns `REEF_FACE_POSITIONS.subList(isRedAlliance ? 6 : 0, +6)`. `ReefSide` further derives left/right branch poses from a face center plus `POLE_DISTANCE` and carries its AprilTag ID, with `otherAlliance(newTagId)` producing the mirrored twin.
patterns.whereSeen: util/Constants.java:937-1147 (FieldConstants) and util/custom/ReefSide.java (74 lines); PoseCalculations.java flipPose/mirrorPose/flipPose3d.
patterns.libraryValue: Alliance flipping is a perennial source of competition-day bugs. The 'author blue, derive red, select by window' pattern is sound and worth generalizing into an `AllianceFlipped<T>` type with a supplier-based accessor — which would also remove the six hand-written `startIndex = isRed ? N : 0` computations that must each be kept in sync with list ordering by hand.

patterns.name: Characterization command suite (wheel radius, static/kS, feedforward regression)
patterns.whatItDoes: Three standalone Commands: `WheelRadiusCharacterization` (spins the drivetrain and back-solves effective wheel radius from gyro vs. wheel rotations), `StaticCharacterization` (ramps current until motion to find kS), and `FeedForwardCharacterization` (collects velocity/voltage samples and fits kS/kV with a `PolynomialRegression` built on the `jama` matrix library). Mechanisms additionally expose full `SysIdRoutine` wrappers.
patterns.whereSeen: commands/characterization/{WheelRadiusCharacterization,StaticCharacterization,FeedForwardCharacterization}.java; util/calc/PolynomialRegression.java (245 lines). SysId helpers at Elevator.java:177-208 (and identical blocks in Wrist/Climb).
patterns.libraryValue: Wheel-radius characterization in particular is high-value and rarely implemented well; it materially improves odometry. PumpkinLib should ship all three plus a standard `sysIdQuasistatic*/sysIdDynamic*` mixin, because the four SysId wrapper methods are copy-pasted verbatim into three subsystems here. Note the honest comment at Elevator.java:180 — "Gaslight SysId since motor is actually running amps instead of volts" — a torque-current-mode SysId adapter would be a genuinely novel library feature.

patterns.name: Sim-driven 3D component poses for AdvantageScope + simulated game pieces
patterns.whatItDoes: Static `Pose3d[] components3d` / `desiredComponents3d` arrays in RobotContainer, indexed by named constants (CLIMB_INDEX=0, ELEVATOR_FIRST_STAGE_INDEX=1, ELEVATOR_SECOND_STAGE_INDEX=2, WRIST_INDEX=3), written from each subsystem's `periodic()` and `setPosition()` so measured and commanded articulation both render. `@AutoLogOutput` publishes them under a `Draggables/` namespace. Simulated coral/algae are parked below the floor and teleported to computed scoring nodes on release, driven by Triggers on `hasPiece()`.
patterns.whereSeen: RobotContainer.java:85-120 (declarations + static initializer) and :248-294 (game-piece Triggers); written from Elevator.java:83-130 and Wrist.java:57-109. Assets: ascope_assets/Robot_{Alpha,Boris,Hugo,Pibble}/model_{0..3}.glb.
patterns.libraryValue: Full-robot 3D visualization is a large driver-practice and debugging win that most teams skip because the wiring is tedious. A library should own the component-pose registry (indexed by a mechanism handle, not a magic int) so subsystems publish articulation without reaching into a static array on RobotContainer — which is the exact coupling that makes this version fragile.

patterns.name: Modular PathPlanner auto composition via generated NamedCommands
patterns.whatItDoes: Autos are assembled by generating 48 NamedCommands in a nested loop (`for reefNode in "ABCDEFGHIJKL" x for level 1..4` → `pathPlannerStorage.autoCycle(node, level)`), each of which races a path-follow against a proximity trigger, waits for a game piece, aligns, places, and returns to a coral station — with the coral station chosen by node letter. Plus ~60 more hand-registered NamedCommands covering distance-gated waits (`WaitUntilShouldRaise`, `WaitUntilShouldLower`) and per-branch alignments.
patterns.whereSeen: util/auto/PathPlannerStorage.java (348 lines, `autoCycle`); RobotContainer.java:470-555 (`prepareNamedCommands`); 252 paths + 17 autos under src/main/deploy/pathplanner.
patterns.libraryValue: The valuable, generalizable idea is *distance-gated command sequencing* — `Commands.waitUntil(pose within X of target)` composed with path following — which decouples mechanism timing from path timing and is far more robust than time-based waits. PumpkinLib should offer this as a `whenWithin(distance, target)` Trigger factory. The generation-loop approach to NamedCommands is also worth blessing, since the hand-written remainder in this repo is where the duplication concentrates.

painPoints.problem: LIVE BUG — `GainConstants` positional-overload collision silently mis-assigns feedforward terms. The 6-double call intended as (P, I, D, FF, minOutput, maxOutput) resolves instead to the Talon overload (P, I, D, S, V, G), so FF is stored as kS, minOutput as kV, and maxOutput as kG — while `getFF()`, `getMinOutput()`, `getMaxOutput()` all return their defaults (0, 0, 0). This is not theoretical: `Neo.setPID(GainConstants, slot)` reads exactly those three getters and pushes them to the SparkMax, so the swerve drive FF of 0.20217 and output range [-1, 1] are silently dropped and replaced by an unintended kS/kV/kG.
painPoints.evidence: util/Constants.java:391-398 `DRIVING_PID = new GainConstants(DRIVING_P, DRIVING_I, DRIVING_D, DRIVING_FF, DRIVING_MIN_OUTPUT, DRIVING_MAX_OUTPUT)` and :406-413 `TURNING_PID` (same shape) — six doubles. The only matching constructor is util/custom/GainConstants.java:56 `public GainConstants(double P, double I, double D, double S, double V, double G)`, which delegates to `this(P, I, D, 0d, S, V, G)`. The FF-carrying constructor at :42 takes only four args and the min/max one at :47 takes five, so neither can match. Consumer: util/hardware/rev/Neo.java:373-384 `setPID(constants.getP(), ..., constants.getFF(), constants.getIZone(), constants.getMinOutput(), constants.getMaxOutput(), slot)`. The identical hazard recurs inside Kraken itself: Kraken.java:968 `setGains(double P,double I,double D,double S,double V,double G)` delegates to `setGains(P, I, D, S, V, G, 0)` — seven doubles — which binds to the 7-arg (P,I,D,A,S,V,G) overload, shifting S→kA, V→kS, G→kV and zeroing kG.
painPoints.libraryFix: Never express gains as a positional double list. PumpkinLib should use a builder or named-field record — `Gains.pid(p,i,d).withKs(..).withKv(..).withKg(..)` — so terms are impossible to transpose and the compiler catches misuse. Provide separate `SparkGains` (FF/iZone/output-range) and `TalonGains` (kS/kV/kA/kG) types rather than one union POJO with eleven fields and eight overlapping constructors, since the union is precisely what makes these silent collisions possible. If a single type is required, forbid multi-double constructors entirely.

painPoints.problem: The entire runtime-tuning capability was built and then commented out rather than switched off, leaving zero tuning path. Changing any gain, any Motion Magic constraint, any vision standard deviation, or any mechanism setpoint requires editing Constants.java, recompiling, and redeploying. There is no SmartDashboard tuning, no `Preferences` usage anywhere in the repo, and the SysId/characterization auto-chooser entries are commented out too.
painPoints.evidence: 30+ commented tunable declarations across 9 files: Vision.java:41-53 (13 consecutive commented `LoggedTunableNumber` std-dev knobs), Elevator.java:47-52 and Wrist.java:46-49 (profile constraints), Swerve.java:70-73, Superstructure.java:45-46, Alignment.java:47-56, and seven commented `LoggedGainConstants` in Constants.java (:242, :256, :507, :523, :608, :669, :781-782). RobotContainer.java:159-173 and :192-218 comment out the gain-push wiring and all 14 SysId/characterization chooser options. Repo-wide: 514 commented lines out of 13,935. `grep -rn Preferences` returns zero hits; SmartDashboard appears only at RobotContainer.java:143 for `Field2d`.
painPoints.libraryFix: Make tunables free and globally gated. A single `PumpkinLib.TUNING_MODE` static final should collapse `TunableNumber.get()` to a plain constant read when false (JIT-eliminated, zero NT traffic), so competition safety never requires commenting code out. Ship the FMS-gating (`!DriverStation.isFMSAttached()`) and `.ignoringDisable(true)` semantics inside the library, and provide a one-liner `tunable.bindTo(io::setGains)` so the push wiring cannot rot into comments.

painPoints.problem: Constants.java is a 1,253-line monolith of ~20 nested classes, mixing CAN IDs, gearing, PID gains, mechanism setpoints, field geometry, controller mappings, and live controller objects. It contains mutable static state and executable logic despite its own header instructing 'Do not put anything functional in this class.' Field geometry alone (lines 924-1252) is ~330 lines of pose math including private helper methods.
painPoints.evidence: util/Constants.java header lines 39-50 says "Do not put anything functional in this class" — yet the file declares mutable `public static HolonomicDriveController TELE_HDC` (:276) and `public static PPHolonomicDriveController AUTO_HDC` (:282), a mutable `public static ArrayList<SparkBase> motors` (:852), two mutable hardware registries `NEO_MOTOR_MAP` (:860) / `KRAKEN_MOTOR_MAP` (:903), a `Map` factory method `initializeMotorGroupMap()` (:875), and private static functions `rotatePose` (:1162), `createCoralPlacementPositions` (:1191), `combineCoralPlacementPositions` (:1208), `flipCoralPlacementPositions` (:1224).
painPoints.libraryFix: PumpkinLib should impose a config layout: per-mechanism config objects (`ElevatorConfig` bundling CAN IDs + gearing + gains + limits + setpoints) that are passed to the IO constructor rather than statically imported, a separate `FieldMap` module for geometry, and a hard rule that runtime registries live in the library (e.g. inside the motor wrapper's own static registry) not in user constants. This also removes the static-init ordering hazard visible here, where `FieldConstants.IS_REAL` is read by `MK4cSwerveModuleConstants.TURNING_P` (:509) from a *later*-declared nested class.

painPoints.problem: Sim-vs-real gains are expressed as seven separate ternary-laden constants per mechanism, then re-bundled — ~50 lines of repetitive declaration per mechanism and no way to see a gain set at a glance.
painPoints.evidence: util/Constants.java:590-606 (Elevator: `P = IS_REAL ? 400d : 1500`, `I`, `D`, `A`, `S`, `V`, `G` then `GAINS = new GainConstants(P,I,D,A,S,V,G)`), :651-667 (Wrist, identical shape), :741-779 (Climb declares fourteen — a full P_SLOW..G_SLOW set and P_FAST..G_FAST set — then bundles into SLOW_GAINS/FAST_GAINS), :509-521 (swerve turning). Several are pure noise: `I = FieldConstants.IS_REAL ? 0d : 0d` appears four times.
painPoints.libraryFix: Provide `Gains.select(real, sim)` returning a whole gain set, so a mechanism declares two readable literals instead of seven ternaries plus a bundling call. Combined with the named-field builder this collapses ~50 lines per mechanism to ~8 and makes the real/sim delta reviewable in a diff.

painPoints.problem: Roughly 500 lines of dead abstractions that still compile, invite edits, and mislead readers about what the robot actually runs. The whole REV/NEO hardware path and the MAXSwerve constants are unreachable from live code.
painPoints.evidence: `LoggedSuperState.java` (42 lines) is never instantiated — grep for `new LoggedSuperState` returns nothing; it is the only *active* consumer of `LoggedTunableNumber`, so the tunable stack has zero live users. `util/calc/OICalc.java` (167 lines) — `toCircle`/`getDistance` are a verbatim character-for-character copy of `PatriBoxController.toCircle`/`getDistance` (compare OICalc.java:21-80 to PatriBoxController.java:167-225) and OICalc is referenced by nothing. `util/custom/Scale3d.java` (73 lines) unreferenced. `commands/managers/HDCTuner.java` (176) is used only by `commands/drive/DriveHDC.java` (110), which is itself never constructed. All five `*IONeo` classes plus `Neo`/`SafeSpark`/`NeoPhysicsSim`/`NeoSimProfile`/`ThroughBoreEncoder` (~1,430 lines) are unreachable — RobotContainer.java:136-140 constructs only `*IOKraken`. `MAXSwerveModuleConstants` (Constants.java:314-419) is dead except that `MK4cSwerveModuleConstants.DRIVING_MOTOR_FREE_SPEED_RPS` and `NeoMotorConstants.VORTEX_FREE_SPEED_RPM` still cross-reference it.
painPoints.libraryFix: If the vendor wrappers live in PumpkinLib behind one common `PumpkinMotor` interface, the per-vendor IO classes collapse from ten files to one parameterized by a motor factory — killing this entire dead-code category structurally. The duplicated `toCircle` is a direct argument for a shared `util.input` module: the copy existed because there was nowhere shared to put it.

painPoints.problem: Per-motor IO boilerplate is mechanical and heavily duplicated: `updateInputs` is a fixed 6-7 line assignment block per motor, repeated across eight IO classes, and `configMotor` repeats the same six-call sequence with different constants.
painPoints.evidence: ElevatorIOKraken.java:38-54 assigns the same seven fields twice (leader + follower, 14 lines). The identical block recurs at WristIOKraken.java:47-53, ClimbIOKraken.java:34-41, CoralClawIOKraken.java:26-32, AlgaeClawIOKraken.java, and ModuleIOKraken.java:93-108. `configMotor` bodies (ElevatorIOKraken.java:19-26, WristIOKraken.java:21-31, ClimbIOKraken.java:18-30) are the same setGearRatio → setUnitConversionFactor → setSoftLimits → setGains → setStatorCurrentLimit → setTorqueCurrentLimits sequence. There is also a real transcription bug in the copy-paste: ModuleIOKraken.java:107 sets `inputs.turnTorqueCurrentAmps = driveMotor.getTorqueCurrentAsDouble()` — reading the **drive** motor into the **turn** input.
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship a `MotorInputs` AutoLog struct plus `inputs.populateFrom(motor)` and a declarative `MotorConfig` applied by one `motor.configure(config)` call. That turns a single-motor IO impl into ~10 lines, makes leader/follower a library concern, and eliminates the copy-paste class that produced the turn/drive mix-up above — which no reviewer would ever catch by eye.

painPoints.problem: Duplicate AdvantageKit log key: the same NT path is published twice by two different mechanisms, which collides at the logger.
painPoints.evidence: subsystems/superstructure/claw/coral/CoralClaw.java:51 `Logger.recordOutput("Subsystems/CoralClaw/HasCoral", hasPiece());` inside `periodic()`, while CoralClaw.java:100 annotates the getter `@AutoLogOutput (key = "Subsystems/CoralClaw/HasCoral")` on `hasPiece()`. Both write the identical key every cycle.
painPoints.libraryFix: PumpkinLib should own logging-key construction (namespace derived from the subsystem instance, leaf name from the field/method) so hand-typed string keys — currently ~60 of them across the repo, several with typos like `"Managers//HDCTuner/..."` (double slash, HDCTuner.java:15) and inconsistent casing `Subsystems/SuperStructure` vs `Subsystems/Superstructure` (Superstructure.java:661 vs :656) — become impossible.

painPoints.problem: Magic numbers with no named constant or derivation, embedded directly in control and simulation logic.
painPoints.evidence: RobotContainer.java:274 `double elevatorHeight = elevator.getPosition()*2+0.776324;` (comment explains it but it is unnamed); RobotContainer.java:241 alignment rumble threshold `< 0.12`; RobotContainer.java:499-506 auto-raise distances `1.9`, `2.6`, `2.0`, `3.5` hardcoded inside NamedCommands; Superstructure.java:194-195 `wrist.getPosition() > 1.6` and `elevator.getPosition() > 0.35`; Superstructure.java:724 endgame threshold `>= 125.0`; ModuleIOKraken.java:95 `>= 1600d` for TalonFX position rollover; Vision.java:134-146 all six pose std-dev values inline (0.001/0.003/0.004, `tagArea > 4.0`, `tagArea > 0.14`) after the tunable versions were commented out; Constants.java:365 `Units.inchesToMeters(1.9160266045332792*2.0)` wheel diameter to 16 significant figures with no provenance; Constants.java:899-915 four signal frequencies each marked `// TODO: FIND THE SWEET SPOT`.
painPoints.libraryFix: Beyond a lint rule, the structural fix is that library-provided mechanisms should take a typed config with named required fields, so thresholds like rollover limits and vision std-devs have a canonical home with library defaults rather than being retyped inline at each call site.

painPoints.problem: Global mutable static state on RobotContainer is written from inside subsystem `periodic()`, creating a circular dependency between the container and its subsystems and making subsystems untestable in isolation.
painPoints.evidence: RobotContainer.java:85-120 declares `public static Pose3d[] components3d`, `desiredComponents3d`, `placedCoral`, `placedAlgae`, `robotPose2d`, `swerveMeasuredStates`, `swerveDesiredStates`, `gameModeStart`, `displayTime`, `placedCoralIndex`. Written from Elevator.java:83-100 and :113-130, Wrist.java:85-90 and :104-109, Swerve.java:228. So `frc.robot.subsystems.superstructure.elevator.Elevator` imports `frc.robot.RobotContainer`. Similarly `Robot.currentTimestamp`/`previousTimestamp`/`gameMode`/`exitAuto` are public mutable statics read from ten files.
painPoints.libraryFix: PumpkinLib should provide a component-pose registry and a robot-state/timing service as injectable singletons owned by the library, so mechanisms publish articulation and read match state through a stable API instead of reaching back into user-level `RobotContainer`/`Robot` statics.

painPoints.problem: Double-brace initialization (anonymous inner subclass per constant) used pervasively for collection constants and even for a live controller object — each creates a hidden subclass, retains an outer reference, and defeats `final`/immutability expectations.
painPoints.evidence: util/Constants.java uses `new ArrayList<Pose2d>() {{ add(...); }}` at :939, :951, :977, :1013, :1083, :1116, :1140, :1246 and `new ArrayList<ReefSide>() {{ ... }}` at :1045; `new HashMap<Integer,String>() {{ put(...); }}` at :862. Most striking is :265-274, where a `ProfiledPIDController` is constructed with a double-brace block to call `setIZone`: `new ProfiledPIDController(...) {{ setIZone(Units.degreesToRadians(45)); }}` — producing an anonymous PID controller subclass used as a shared static. Separately, `AutoConstants.XY_PID` (:258) is a single `PIDController` instance passed as **both** the X and Y controller of `TELE_HDC` (:276-280), so both axes share one controller's internal integral/derivative state.
painPoints.libraryFix: Provide `List.of(...)`-style factories and a `FieldMap` builder so users never reach for double-brace init, and have the library construct holonomic controllers from a gains config — which would structurally prevent aliasing one PIDController across two axes (a subtle correctness bug that produces cross-axis coupling in auto-align).

painPoints.problem: Massive near-identical repetition in auto wiring: 12 `Align{A..L}` plus 6 `PAlign{E..J}` NamedCommands differing only in index and a boolean, and a `PathPlannerStorage.autoCycle` switch whose case bodies are ~30-line copies differing by one string.
painPoints.evidence: RobotContainer.java:510-528 registers 18 alignment NamedCommands of the form `alignment.autonomousReefAutoAlignmentCommand(() -> FieldConstants.GET_REEF_FACE_POSITIONS().get(N), bool).onlyIf(() -> coralClaw.hasPiece()).withTimeout(3.0)`. util/auto/PathPlannerStorage.java:62-140+ switches on reef node with cases 'J', 'E', 'A', ... whose bodies are copies differing only in the `WaitUntilShouldRaiseX` string. RobotContainer.java:497 re-registers `"Stow"` (already registered at :476) and :498 registers `"PrepL4"` bound to `superstructure.L2` — a likely copy-paste error. Alignment.java:297 carries the comment `// TODO: Make this less 🤮 because MY LORD`.
painPoints.libraryFix: The generation loop the team already uses for the 48 level/node commands (RobotContainer.java:530-539) is the right answer; the library should push teams toward it with a `NamedCommandRegistry` that registers parameterized families and *rejects duplicate names* — which would have caught both the double `"Stow"` registration and the mismatched `"PrepL4"`.

painPoints.problem: No unit types anywhere — every quantity is a raw `double` with units encoded in the identifier, so unit mismatches are invisible to the compiler despite WPILib's Units API being available and even pre-configured in the editor.
painPoints.evidence: Names carry the units: `L4_POSITION_METERS`, `MIN_ANGLE_RADIANS`, `VELOCITY_DEADBAND_RADIANS`, `CURRENT_THRESHOLD_HAS_PIECE_AMPS`, `TALONFX_FAST_UPDATE_FREQ_HZ`. `.vscode/settings.json` lists `edu.wpi.first.units.Units.*` as a favorite static import, and Elevator.java:11-13 imports `Second`/`Seconds`/`Volts` — but only for the SysId routine (Elevator.java:181-187); no mechanism API is unit-typed. `Kraken.setTargetPosition(double position)` is documented as "position / PCF give rotations", pushing unit correctness entirely onto the caller.
painPoints.libraryFix: Adopt WPILib `Distance`/`Angle`/`AngularVelocity`/`Current` in PumpkinLib's public mechanism and config APIs (`setPosition(Distance)`), keeping raw doubles only in hot internal paths. This is the highest-leverage correctness change available for a shared library, and it subsumes the entire unit-conversion-factor concern that `Kraken` currently handles by convention and documentation.

painPoints.problem: Dead enum branches and unused capability in the hardware wrappers indicate the abstraction surface outgrew its use, with no compiler signal.
painPoints.evidence: `Kraken.TelemetryPreference.NO_ENCODER` is documented "Intake roller, for example" (Kraken.java:179) but is never selected: the only `setTelemetryPreference` calls in mechanism code are `TelemetryPreference.SWERVE` at ModuleIOKraken.java:55-56. The claw IOs — the exact rollers the enum was written for — never call it, so they run `DEFAULT` and pay for position/velocity signals at 50Hz they do not use. `Kraken` also exposes `MM_VOLTAGE`/`MM_TORQUE_CURRENT` control preferences and a full `configureMotionMagic`, but only `ClimbIOKraken.java:28` ever configures Motion Magic while every mechanism constructs with `ControlPreference.TORQUE_CURRENT` — so the Motion Magic request objects are allocated and never used.
painPoints.libraryFix: Derive telemetry/signal configuration from the declared mechanism type rather than an opt-in enum — a `RollerMechanism` should not subscribe to position signals at all, by construction. That both removes the footgun of forgetting the call and delivers the CAN savings automatically, which is the stated goal of the enum in the first place.

constraints: Java 17 exactly (build.gradle sets sourceCompatibility/targetCompatibility to VERSION_17; CI pins Temurin 17). PumpkinLib must not require Java 21+ language features — records and arrow-switch are fine, but no pattern matching for switch, no sealed-interface exhaustiveness beyond 17, no virtual threads.

Must compose with AdvantageKit (4.1.2) rather than fight it: the library must not break log-replay determinism. Concretely, library code must route all hardware reads through the IO layer, must not read wall-clock or nondeterministic sources outside IO, and must expose `@AutoLog`-compatible input structs.
