The `akit-autolog` annotation processor is wired in build.gradle by parsing the vendordep JSON version, so any library-provided AutoLog structs must work with that processor.

Must support both CTRE Phoenix 6 (TalonFX/Kraken X60, CANcoder, Pigeon2) and REV (SparkMax/SparkFlex, NEO/Vortex) behind one interface — this team maintains full parallel implementations of every mechanism for both vendors and pays ~1,400 lines for the privilege. Vendor-neutral motor abstraction is a hard requirement, not a nice-to-have.

Must not add CAN-bus load. This codebase deliberately manages status-signal update frequencies per motor role, calls `optimizeBusUtilization(0, timeout)` on every Kraken, uses `withUpdateFreqHz(0)` one-shot control requests, and runs the drivetrain on a separate 'Drivebase' CAN bus. Any library abstraction that subscribes to signals a mechanism does not use is a regression.

Must be competition-safe by default: tunables must be gated by `!DriverStation.isFMSAttached()` and must cost nothing when tuning is off. The evidence that this matters is that this team commented out its entire tunable stack by hand rather than ship it to competition — a library that forces that tradeoff will be disabled the same way.

Must tolerate real hardware failure at boot: config application must be retried and read-back-verified (the `DeviceUtil.applyParameter` contract), and must degrade gracefully in simulation (that helper short-circuits when `IS_SIMULATION`). Sensor loss must not be fatal — see WristIOKraken.java:35-44 and ModuleIOKraken.java:110-117, which both fall back to the internal encoder when the absolute encoder is disconnected.

Must run under a 100MB fixed JVM heap with SerialGC and `AlwaysPreTouch` (build.gradle:32-40, settings inherited from teams 254/6328). No per-loop allocation in hot paths — note this codebase mutates pre-allocated `SwerveModuleState`/`TrapezoidProfile.State` objects in place rather than reallocating, and pre-allocates all CTRE control requests in the constructor.

Must keep the 20ms loop budget: the team escalates main-thread RT priority (RobotContainer.threadRTCommand, deferred 20s after robotInit per a ChiefDelphi thread on auto-init overrun) and wrote `PatriBoxController` partly to dodge a WPILib loop-overrun issue. Library periodic work must be bounded and cheap.

Must support REAL / SIM / REPLAY as first-class modes (Constants.LoggingConstants.Mode) and a robot-identity concept (RobotType DEVBOT/COMPBOT/SIMBOT) that selects gains and behavior, including the guard that auto-corrects SIMBOT→COMPBOT when running on real hardware.

Must integrate with PathPlanner 2025 (AutoBuilder.configure, NamedCommands, PPHolonomicDriveController, SwerveSetpointGenerator, RobotConfig.fromGUISettings) — 252 paths and 17 autos already exist in src/main/deploy/pathplanner, so the auto layer cannot require re-authoring paths.

Preserve the author's evident style: 4-space indentation (exactly one tab character in the whole 13,935-line codebase), K&R braces, SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE constants in nested `public static final class` blocks, camelCase members, arrow-switch expressions (43 uses), `d`-suffixed double literals (450d, 1500d), Javadoc on hardware/util public methods, units spelled out in identifier names, and a tolerance for humor in comments ('Warm up PathPlanner, he starts off cold', 'check in on him :)'). There is no CLAUDE.md, no formatter config, and no checkstyle — style is conveyed by convention only.

Must remain readable and modifiable by high-school students mid-season under time pressure. This repo is explicitly 'entirely student-created and maintained' with an Agile/sprint workflow (README). Heavy generics, deep inheritance, or annotation-processor magic beyond the AdvantageKit norm will not survive contact with a 2am pit debugging session — the fact that this team's own most sophisticated abstraction (the tunable stack) is the one that got commented out is the cautionary data point.

source: Web research (28+ primary sources): FRC simulation & testing ecosystem, 2026 REBUILT season retrospective + WPILib 2027/Systemcore preview. Sources: docs.wpilib.org (stable/2026 and /en/2027), github.wpilib.org allwpilib Javadocs, allwpilib GitHub raw files at tags v2026.2.1 and v2027.0.0-alpha-6, maple-sim GitHub + GitHub REST API + docs site, CTRE Phoenix 6 docs + changelog API, REV REVLib docs, PhotonVision docs + Javadocs, AdvantageKit docs, AdvantageScope docs, Elastic dashboard GitBook, Limelight docs, gregk27/FRC-CI-Demo, OHS-Robotics/Spartobots-2026.
summary: FRC simulation in 2026 is a three-layer stack that no single library unifies: (1) WPILib physics sims (`LinearSystemSim` subclasses — `DCMotorSim`, `ElevatorSim`, `SingleJointedArmSim`, `FlywheelSim`, plus `DifferentialDrivetrainSim` and `BatterySim`) which model a mechanism but know nothing about your motor controller; (2) vendor SimState bridges (Phoenix 6 `TalonFXSimState`/`CANcoderSimState`, REVLib `SparkMaxSim`/`SparkFlexSim`, generic `SimDeviceSim`) which each expose a *different API shape* and must be hand-glued to layer 1 every single time; (3) maple-sim, which adds dyn4j rigid-body physics for the full field, game pieces, intakes and projectiles — its 2026 REBUILT support (`RebuiltFuelOnField`, `RebuiltFuelOnFly`, `setHitTargetCallBack`) is real and documented, but shipped only as **v0.4.0-beta (published 2026-01-17)**; the GitHub `releases/latest` endpoint still returns the 2025-era v0.3.14, so 2026 support was never promoted to stable. The single largest source of duplicated code across every FRC repo is the ~40-line `simulationPeriodic()` glue block per mechanism (read vendor sim voltage → feed WPILib sim → write rotor position/velocity back, remembering that vendor rotor units are *pre*-gear-ratio while `DCMotorSim` returns *post*-gear-ratio) — this is the highest-value thing PumpkinLib can absorb. Unit testing is well-supported but under-documented and full of timing footguns: JUnit 5 ships in GradleRIO, tests need `assert HAL.initialize(500, 0)`, subsystems must implement `AutoCloseable`, and Phoenix 6 specifically requires `DriverStationSim.setEnabled(true)` + `DriverStation.notifyNewData()` plus a ~100 ms settle after construction and ~20 ms after each control request; `SimHooks.pauseTiming()`/`stepTiming()` gives deterministic time but there is no WPILib-provided harness that ticks `simulationPeriodic()` or the `CommandScheduler` for you. The dominant 2027 constraint dwarfs everything else: Systemcore replaces the roboRIO, Java moves to 25, all Java packages move `edu.wpi.first` → `org.wpilib`, Commands v3 (coroutine-based) lands alongside deprecated Commands v2, Shuffleboard/SmartDashboard/PathWeaver/RobotBuilder are deleted, NetworkTables v3 is removed, `robotInit()` and per-vendor gamepad classes are gone, `MotorController.set()` becomes `setThrottle()`, and "Test" mode is renamed "Utility" — so any library written for 2026 needs a deliberate dual-target or migration story, and PumpkinLib's public API should avoid hard-coding names that 2027 renames.
stack:
**WPILib 2026** (current stable line 2026.2.1/2026.2.2; Java packages `edu.wpi.first.*`). Sim classes live in `edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.simulation`: `LinearSystemSim` (base), `DCMotorSim`, `ElevatorSim`, `SingleJointedArmSim`, `FlywheelSim`, `DifferentialDrivetrainSim` (only one NOT deriving from `LinearSystemSim`), `BatterySim`, `RoboRioSim`, `DriverStationSim`, `EncoderSim`, `PWMSim`/`PWMMotorControllerSim`, `DIOSim`, `AnalogInputSim`, `DoubleSolenoidSim`, `SimDeviceSim`, `SimHooks`. Docs: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/physics-sim.html , https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/device-sim.html , API index https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/release/java/edu/wpi/first/wpilibj/simulation/package-summary.html
**WPILib 2027 (alpha, Systemcore)** — tag `v2027.0.0-alpha-6` exists on GitHub; docs at https://docs.wpilib.org/en/2027/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html . Java 25 / C++23; `edu.wpi.first` → `org.wpilib` (e.g. `org.wpilib.hardware.hal.HAL`, `org.wpilib.simulation.PWMMotorControllerSim`); NT3 removed; new `Gamepad` class replaces `XboxController`/`PS4Controller`; `Commands v3` in `org.wpilib.commands3` (coroutine/continuation-based, requires Java 21+ features unavailable on roboRIO — https://github.com/wpilibsuite/allwpilib/blob/main/design-docs/commands-v3.md ); onboard IMU sim added. Removed for Systemcore: relay, analog output, analog gyro, SPI + SPI IMUs (ADIS16448/16470/ADXRS450/ADXL345), DMA, Counter, AnalogTrigger, DigitalGlitchFilter, interrupts, ultrasonic, servo, built-in accelerometer (https://docs.wpilib.org/en/2027/docs/yearly-overview/removed-features.html).
**Motor controllers / CAN — CTRE Phoenix 6**: 2026 line `26.1.x` (26.1.0 kickoff; 26.1.2 on 2026/03/11); 2027 alpha line `26.50.0-alpha-1` (2026/06/12). Sim API: `device.getSimState()` → `TalonFXSimState` (`setSupplyVoltage`, `getMotorVoltageMeasure`, `setRawRotorPosition`, `setRotorVelocity`, `setMotorType` [new 26.0.0-beta-1: KrakenX60 ↔ KrakenX44], `Orientation`/`ChassisReference`), `CANcoderSimState` (+ `SensorOffset`, new 26.0.0-beta-1), `TalonFXSSimState.PulseWidthSensorOffset`, `CANdiSimState.Pwm*SensorOffset`, `Pigeon2SimState`, `SimSwerveDrivetrain` (default drive inertia raised to 0.035 kg·m² in 26.1.2). Docs https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/simulation/simulation-intro.html ; changelog https://api.ctr-electronics.com/changelog
**Motor controllers — REVLib**: `com.revrobotics.sim` / `com.revrobotics.spark.sparksim` — `SparkSim` (base) → `SparkMaxSim`, `SparkFlexSim`; also `SparkRelativeEncoderSim`, `SparkAbsoluteEncoderSim`, `SparkSimFaultManager`. Core method `iterate(velocityRPM, busVoltage, dtSeconds)`. Docs https://docs.revrobotics.com/revlib/spark/sim/simulation-getting-started ; API https://codedocs.revrobotics.com/java/com/revrobotics/sim/package-summary
**Full-field physics — maple-sim** (Shenzhen Robotics Alliance; Team 5516 "Iron Maple" + 6706 "Golem"). Wraps **dyn4j 5.0.2** 2D rigid-body engine. Vendordep: `https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/vendordep/maple-sim.json`. Packages: `drivesims`, `motorsims`, `gamepieces`, `seasonspecific`, `utils`. Repo https://github.com/Shenzhen-Robotics-Alliance/maple-sim ; docs https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/
**Vision sim — PhotonVision** (`org.photonvision.simulation`): `VisionSystemSim`, `PhotonCameraSim`, `SimCameraProperties`, `VisionTargetSim`, `TargetModel`. 2026 releases confirmed in Javadocs (v2026.1.1, v2026.3.4). https://docs.photonvision.org/en/latest/docs/simulation/simulation-java.html
**Logging / replay**: WPILib `DataLogManager` + **Epilogue** (`edu.wpi.first.epilogue`, `@Logged` annotation processor, `Epilogue.bind()` on `TimedRobot`); **AdvantageKit 2026** (IO-layer + deterministic replay, `@AutoLog`, `Logger.processInputs`); **AdvantageScope 2026** (27.0.0-alpha-4 referenced for 2027). https://docs.advantagekit.org/whats-new/ , https://docs.advantagescope.org/whats-new/
**Dashboards**: Elastic 2026.x (2027.0.0-alpha-8 referenced by WPILib 2027) — has a first-class **Alerts** widget consuming the WPILib Alert API. https://frc-elastic.gitbook.io/docs/additional-features-and-references/widgets-list-and-properties-reference
**Test/CI**: JUnit 5 (bundled in GradleRIO), Google Test for C++; GitHub Actions with container `wpilib/roborio-cross-ubuntu:2025-22.04` on `ubuntu-22.04`. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/advanced-gradlerio/robot-code-ci.html
**Characterization**: `edu.wpi.first.wpilibj2.command.sysid.SysIdRoutine` + `edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.sysid.SysIdRoutineLog`.
**No sim support**: Limelight / LimelightLib — see painPoints.

patterns.name: Mechanism sim glue: WPILib physics sim ↔ vendor SimState
patterns.whatItDoes: The universal per-subsystem `simulationPeriodic()` block: push battery voltage into the vendor sim state, pull the vendor's applied motor voltage out, step a WPILib `LinearSystemSim` subclass by 20 ms, then write the resulting position/velocity back into the vendor sim so the vendor's own onboard PID and current limiting behave correctly. This exact shape is re-typed once per mechanism in essentially every FRC repo.
patterns.whereSeen: CTRE: https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/simulation/simulation-intro.html | REV: https://docs.revrobotics.com/revlib/spark/sim/simulation-getting-started | WPILib: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/physics-sim.html
patterns.libraryValue: HIGHEST-VALUE ITEM. Three vendors expose three incompatible sim idioms (CTRE: setter-based rotor writes; REV: a single `iterate(rpm, volts, dt)` call; everything else: stringly-typed `SimDeviceSim` keys). A `PumpkinSim.arm/elevator/flywheel/roller(...)` factory that auto-detects the motor controller type and hides the rotor-vs-mechanism gear-ratio conversion removes ~40 lines of error-prone boilerplate per mechanism and eliminates the single most common silent sim bug (gear ratio applied on the wrong side, which makes vendor-side PID tuning in sim meaningless).

patterns.name: SimDeviceSim escape hatch for unsupported vendors
patterns.whatItDoes: Generic simulation for any vendor device that registered a `SimDevice` but has no dedicated sim class. Devices appear in SimGUI's 'Other Devices' tab. Accessed by a stringly-typed key of the form `Prefix:Device Name[index]`.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/device-sim.html | https://github.com/wpilibsuite/frc-docs/blob/main/source/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/device-sim.rst
patterns.libraryValue: PumpkinLib should ship a thin typed wrapper + a discovery/dump utility (`PumpkinSim.dumpDevices()` printing every registered SimDevice key and field) so teams can wire up a no-sim-support vendor in minutes instead of guessing key strings. This is the documented fallback path for anything CTRE/REV/WPILib don't cover.

patterns.name: maple-sim SimulatedArena — full-field physics with game pieces
patterns.whatItDoes: Singleton dyn4j world that owns drivetrain bodies, game pieces, intakes and projectiles. Runs sub-ticks decoupled from the robot loop (default 5 sub-ticks per 0.02 s period = 250 Hz physics). Provides real collisions between robot bumpers, field elements and game pieces, plus scoring callbacks.
patterns.whereSeen: https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/using-the-simulated-arena/ | https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/rebuilt/ | https://github.com/Shenzhen-Robotics-Alliance/maple-sim
patterns.libraryValue: maple-sim is the only thing in FRC that lets a small team validate an *entire autonomous scoring cycle* — drive, intake a real game piece, shoot it, confirm it scored — with zero robot time. But its 2026 support is beta-only and setup is nontrivial. PumpkinLib should (a) provide a one-call opt-in wrapper that registers the arena tick, guards it behind `RobotBase.isSimulation()`, and auto-publishes game-piece `Pose3d[]` to AdvantageScope; (b) degrade gracefully to plain WPILib sims when maple-sim is absent, so the dependency is optional rather than load-bearing.

patterns.name: maple-sim projectile + scoring callback (shooter tuning without a field)
patterns.whatItDoes: Models a launched game piece as a ballistic projectile carrying the chassis velocity, with target-hit detection and trajectory display callbacks. Lets you tune shooter velocity/angle/lead-compensation against simulated scoring outcomes.
patterns.whereSeen: https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/simulating-projectiles/ | https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/rebuilt/
patterns.codeSketch:
SimulatedArena.getInstance().addGamePieceProjectile(
  new RebuiltFuelOnFly(
      driveSimulation.getSimulatedDriveTrainPose().getTranslation(), // chassis position
      shooterOffset,                 // Translation2d, shooter vs robot center
      chassisSpeedsFieldRelative,    // robot velocity is ADDED to the projectile
      shooterHeading,                // Rotation2d = robot heading + shooter rotation
      initialHeightMeters,
      launchVelocityMetersPerSec,
      launchAngleRadians)
    .withTargetPosition(() -> HUB_POSE)
    .withTargetTolerance(new Translation3d(0.2, 0.2, 0.3))
    .withHitTargetCallBack(() -> System.out.println("FUEL hits HUB!"))
    .withProjectileTrajectoryDisplayCallBack(
        hitPoses  -> Logger.recordOutput("Shot/Success", hitPoses.toArray(Pose3d[]::new)),
        missPoses -> Logger.recordOutput("Shot/Miss",    missPoses.toArray(Pose3d[]::new)))
    .enableBecomesGamePieceOnFieldAfterTouchGround());
patterns.libraryValue: This is the concrete answer to 'we can't tune the shooter because we have no field time.' PumpkinLib can wrap this into a `ShotSolver`/`ShooterTuner` that sweeps velocity×angle in sim, records hit rate, and emits an interpolating lookup table — turning days of field iteration into a headless sweep. Note the tuned gravity constant (11 m/s², not 9.81) means maple-sim projectiles are empirically fudged, so treat outputs as a starting point, not truth.

patterns.name: maple-sim hardware-abstraction swerve (run real subsystem code against sim physics)
patterns.whatItDoes: Two documented fidelity tiers. 'Simple' embeds control inside maple-sim (fast to adopt, diverges from real robot code). 'Hardware abstraction' runs the *exact same* subsystem/controller code against simulated motors, so what you tune in sim transfers to the robot.
patterns.whereSeen: https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/swerve-simulation-overview/ | https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/swerve-sim-hardware-abstraction/
patterns.libraryValue: Validates the IO-layer pattern as the correct seam for a sim-capable library: if PumpkinLib's subsystems talk to a narrow hardware interface, maple-sim, WPILib sims, and real hardware all become interchangeable implementations. Also note WPILib itself still ships no swerve physics sim — the 2027 docs source still reads "Swerve support for simulation is in the works" — so swerve sim is a genuine third-party-only gap PumpkinLib could fill or wrap.

patterns.name: JUnit 5 subsystem test harness (HAL init + AutoCloseable)
patterns.whatItDoes: The canonical WPILib unit-test shape: initialize the HAL, construct the subsystem, attach sim objects, assert on sim outputs, and free HAL allocations in teardown. Failing to close leaks HAL port allocations and makes the *next* test fail with a confusing 'port already allocated' error.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/unit-testing.html | 2026: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wpilibsuite/allwpilib/v2026.2.1/wpilibjExamples/src/test/java/edu/wpi/first/wpilibj/examples/unittest/subsystems/IntakeTest.java | 2027 alpha: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wpilibsuite/allwpilib/v2027.0.0-alpha-6/wpilibjExamples/src/test/java/org/wpilib/examples/unittest/subsystems/IntakeTest.java
patterns.libraryValue: PumpkinLib should ship a JUnit 5 base class / extension (`@ExtendWith(PumpkinRobotTest.class)` or `PumpkinTestBase`) that does HAL init, DS enable, timing pause, subsystem registration and guaranteed close — turning a 25-line boilerplate preamble into one annotation. Small teams do not write tests today largely because this preamble is undocumented tribal knowledge and its failure modes (leaked HAL ports, disabled actuators) are inscrutable.

patterns.name: Deterministic-time testing with SimHooks (pause/step/resume)
patterns.whatItDoes: Detaches simulated time from wall clock so control-loop tests are fast and repeatable. Without it, tests either sleep in real time (slow, flaky in CI) or never advance time at all (controllers never converge).
patterns.whereSeen: https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/release/java/edu/wpi/first/wpilibj/simulation/package-summary.html | known bug: https://github.com/wpilibsuite/allwpilib/issues/6641
patterns.libraryValue: This is the mechanism that makes 'test the whole subsystem including its controller' viable in CI. PumpkinLib should expose `PumpkinTest.runFor(Seconds.of(4), subsystem)` that ticks periodic + simulationPeriodic + CommandScheduler + stepTiming in the right order. The ordering is unobvious and there is no WPILib helper for it — every team reinvents it or gives up.

patterns.name: Vendor-specific test enablement (Phoenix 6 settle delays)
patterns.whatItDoes: Simulated actuators are gated on DS-enabled state, and Phoenix devices need real settle time before they respond. Skipping this produces tests that assert 0.0 and fail mysteriously.
patterns.whereSeen: https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/wpilib-integration/unit-testing.html
patterns.libraryValue: Pure tribal knowledge buried in vendor docs; costs teams entire evenings. PumpkinLib's test base class should encode DS-enable + the documented settle delays automatically, and its sim harness should bump Phoenix signal update frequencies in sim (CTRE explicitly recommends higher rates + a `Notifier` for better simulated PID).

patterns.name: GitHub Actions CI for robot code
patterns.whatItDoes: Builds and runs the full JUnit suite on every push/PR inside the official WPILib cross-compile container. `./gradlew build` compiles robot code AND runs tests.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/advanced-gradlerio/robot-code-ci.html | https://docs.wpilib.org/en/2027/_sources/docs/software/advanced-gradlerio/robot-code-ci.rst.txt
patterns.codeSketch:
name: CI
on:
  push: { branches: [ main ] }
  pull_request: { branches: [ main ] }
jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
    container: wpilib/roborio-cross-ubuntu:2025-22.04   # JDK + C++ + roboRIO toolchains
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v6
    - name: Add repository to git safe directories
      run: git config --global --add safe.directory $GITHUB_WORKSPACE
    - name: Grant execute permission for gradlew
      run: chmod +x gradlew
    - name: Compile and run tests on robot code
      run: ./gradlew build

# Note: the 2025 image tag is still correct for 2026 (dependencies unchanged
# between 2025 and 2026 per WPILib docs).
patterns.libraryValue: PumpkinLib should ship this workflow as a template file in its project scaffold, plus a `pumpkinCheck` gradle task aggregating build + test + format. Near-zero cost, and it is the only thing that keeps a small team's tests from silently rotting. Real-world reference: gregk27/FRC-CI-Demo adds Checkstyle as a third CI gate (https://github.com/gregk27/FRC-CI-Demo).

patterns.name: IO-layer hardware abstraction (AdvantageKit style)
patterns.whatItDoes: Subsystems depend on a narrow IO interface, never on hardware classes. Implementations: Real (TalonFX/Spark), Sim (WPILib/maple-sim), and Replay (empty — inputs come from the log). Inputs are logged as a struct each cycle, which is what makes deterministic replay possible.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/recording-inputs/io-interfaces/ | https://docs.advantagekit.org/theory/log-replay-comparison/
patterns.libraryValue: The seam that makes sim, replay, and real hardware interchangeable — and the same seam maple-sim's 'hardware abstraction' tier expects. PumpkinLib should adopt an IO-shaped architecture even if it does NOT depend on AdvantageKit, so teams can bolt AdvantageKit on later without rewriting. Consider generating the Real/Sim pair from one declaration to kill the 3x-implementation tax that makes small teams abandon the pattern.

patterns.name: Deterministic log replay for off-robot re-tuning
patterns.whatItDoes: Re-runs the exact recorded inputs through (possibly modified) robot code off-robot, producing outputs identical to what the real robot would have done. Enables tuning between matches with no robot access.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.advantagekit.org/theory/log-replay-comparison/ | https://docs.advantagekit.org/theory/deterministic-timestamps/
patterns.libraryValue: Directly serves 'small teams have little robot time': every disabled/practice/match run becomes a re-runnable test fixture. PumpkinLib should (a) never call `Timer.getFPGATimestamp()` in control paths, (b) accept an injectable clock so replay and unit tests can drive time, (c) consider shipping recorded logs as regression fixtures. Note AdvantageKit explicitly scopes its comparison to replay-capable tools and states WPILib DataLog and Epilogue are non-replay logging — they are complementary, not competitors.

patterns.name: Epilogue annotation telemetry + DataLogManager (zero-ceremony logging)
patterns.whatItDoes: `@Logged` on a class triggers a compile-time annotation processor that logs every field and every public no-arg accessor. `Epilogue.bind()` on a TimedRobot adds a periodic logging call at loop rate, phase-offset by half a cycle to avoid contending with control loops. `DataLogManager.start()` mirrors NT data to disk with automatic file rotation and match-number naming.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/telemetry/robot-telemetry-with-annotations.html | https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/release/java/edu/wpi/first/wpilibj/DataLogManager.html
patterns.libraryValue: The right default for a small-team library: near-zero-effort logging with no IO-layer discipline required. PumpkinLib should make its own types Epilogue-friendly (public no-arg accessors returning loggable/struct/protobuf types) and annotate defensively — this is strictly cheaper for small teams than full AdvantageKit adoption, and is the recommended on-ramp before graduating to replay.

patterns.name: PhotonVision VisionSystemSim — the only real camera sim in FRC
patterns.whatItDoes: Simulates AprilTag/object detection end-to-end including calibration error, FPS, and latency distribution, feeding results into the real `PhotonCamera` object so pose-estimation code is exercised unchanged. Publishes a `Field2d` to NT at `/VisionSystemSim-[label]/Sim Field`.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.photonvision.org/en/latest/docs/simulation/simulation-java.html | https://javadocs.photonvision.org/release/org/photonvision/simulation/package-summary.html
patterns.libraryValue: Latency and calibration-error modeling means vision *filtering and rejection* logic (std-dev scaling, ambiguity gates, stale-measurement rejection) can be regression-tested headlessly — historically the hardest FRC code to validate without a field. PumpkinLib should wrap this with sane defaults per camera model and auto-disable streams when headless/CI is detected. This also creates a strong reason to prefer PhotonVision over Limelight in PumpkinLib's recommended stack.

patterns.name: SysIdRoutine characterization plumbed as commands
patterns.whatItDoes: Standard quasistatic (voltage ramp) + dynamic (voltage step) tests that emit SysId-compatible logs for feedforward/feedback gain extraction. Exposed as commands so they can be bound to buttons or sequenced in auto.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/advanced-controls/system-identification/creating-routine.html | https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/release/java/edu/wpi/first/wpilibj2/command/sysid/SysIdRoutine.html | AdvantageKit compat: https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/sysid-compatibility/ | CTRE: https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/wpilib-integration/sysid-integration/plumbing-and-running-sysid.html
patterns.libraryValue: Characterization is exactly the 'burns scarce robot time' activity PumpkinLib targets. Two concrete wins: (1) auto-generate the SysId plumbing from the same mechanism declaration used to build the sim, so teams write it once; (2) run SysId *against the sim* to validate the routine and the safety limits before ever putting it on a real mechanism — catching wrong-direction / wrong-units mistakes that otherwise destroy hardware.

patterns.name: Alert API as the self-test / health-check substrate
patterns.whatItDoes: Persistent, typed, NT-published fault reporting. Created once and toggled, not spammed. Published under `/SmartDashboard/<Group>` (defaults to group `Alerts`); multiple groups allow separate widgets. Elastic renders these in a dedicated Alerts widget.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/telemetry/persistent-alerts.html | https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/release/java/edu/wpi/first/wpilibj/Alert.html | https://frc-elastic.gitbook.io/docs/additional-features-and-references/widgets-list-and-properties-reference
patterns.libraryValue: There is NO standard FRC health-check framework — every team hand-rolls it or (usually) skips it, then loses matches to a disconnected CAN device nobody noticed. A `PumpkinHealth` registry that auto-registers per-device checks (connected, sticky faults, encoder-sane, temperature, brownout, CAN utilization) and surfaces them as grouped Alerts is a high-value, low-effort differentiator that works on real hardware AND in sim. Isolate the Alert API behind a PumpkinLib facade given the documented instability warning.

patterns.name: Hardware fault/health signal sources to aggregate
patterns.whatItDoes: The concrete readable signals a health-check layer should poll, across WPILib and vendors.
patterns.whereSeen: https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/release/java/edu/wpi/first/wpilibj/RobotController.html | https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/can-devices/power-distribution-module.html | https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/roborio-info/roborio-brownouts.html | https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/2024/docs/api-reference/api-usage/faults.html
patterns.libraryValue: Gives the health registry a concrete, citable checklist. The REVLib `SparkSimFaultManager` point is especially useful: PumpkinLib can ship tests that inject faults in sim and assert the right Alert fires — making the health layer itself testable rather than aspirational.

painPoints.problem: Per-mechanism sim glue is copy-pasted N times per robot, and the rotor-vs-mechanism gear-ratio conversion is a silent correctness trap
painPoints.evidence: CTRE's own docs annotate the trap verbatim: "note that this is rotor position/velocity (before gear ratio), but DCMotorSim returns mechanism position/velocity (after gear ratio)" — https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/simulation/simulation-intro.html . REVLib's equivalent is a totally different call, `flexSim.iterate(rpm, RoboRioSim.getVInVoltage(), 0.02)` requiring a manual rad/s→RPM conversion — https://docs.revrobotics.com/revlib/spark/sim/simulation-getting-started . Every arm/elevator/flywheel/roller repeats ~40 lines of this.
painPoints.libraryFix: A vendor-agnostic `PumpkinSim.arm(...)/.elevator(...)/.flywheel(...)/.roller(...)` builder that takes the mechanism's physical description ONCE (gearing, MOI/mass, limits, motor) and auto-detects the controller type to emit the correct glue. Gear ratio is applied internally on the correct side. Wrong units become impossible because the builder takes WPILib `Measure` types (Kilograms, Meters, Degrees) rather than bare doubles.

painPoints.problem: Three vendors, three incompatible sim idioms — and no unified way to say 'simulate this mechanism'
painPoints.evidence: Phoenix 6 uses setter-based rotor writes on a SimState object (`setSupplyVoltage`, `setRawRotorPosition`, `setRotorVelocity`, plus an `Orientation`/`ChassisReference` field independent of runtime invert). REVLib uses one `iterate(velocityRPM, busVoltage, dt)` call. Anything else uses stringly-typed `SimDeviceSim("Prefix:Device Name[index]")` lookups where a missing prefix silently fails to match (https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/device-sim.html).
painPoints.libraryFix: Define a small internal `SimulatedMotor` SPI with Real/TalonFX/SparkMax/SparkFlex/SimDevice implementations, mirroring how maple-sim abstracts via `SimulatedMotorController`. Teams that mix CTRE and REV (very common on small budgets) then write identical subsystem code for both.

painPoints.problem: Battery sag and brownout are not modeled unless you wire them yourself, so sim never reproduces the failure mode that actually loses matches
painPoints.evidence: `BatterySim` exists as a separate opt-in class that "estimates battery voltage sag based on drawn currents", and it only affects anything if you push its result into `RoboRioSim.setVInVoltage(...)` and read it back via `RoboRioSim.getVInVoltage()` — https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/physics-sim.html . Nothing does this by default; CTRE's own example just hardcodes `setSupplyVoltage(RobotController.getBatteryVoltage())`. Real brownout threshold is 6.75 V on roboRIO 2.0 (https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/roborio-info/roborio-brownouts.html).
painPoints.libraryFix: PumpkinLib auto-registers every simulated mechanism with a global current-draw aggregator, computes sag via `BatterySim`, and pushes it to `RoboRioSim.setVInVoltage()` — for free, with no user code. Ship a `PumpkinSim.stressTest()` that runs all mechanisms at max simultaneously and reports predicted sag/brownout, so small teams find power problems before the field does.

painPoints.problem: Nothing calls simulationPeriodic() or CommandScheduler.run() inside a unit test — so sim-backed subsystem tests silently do nothing
painPoints.evidence: WPILib docs describe `simulationPeriodic()` as being called by the TimedRobot loop or overridden on command-based `Subsystem` (https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/physics-sim.html), but the official unit-test example (IntakeTest.java) tests only instantaneous setters and never advances a control loop at all. `SimHooks.pauseTiming()/stepTiming()` exist but appear in no official unit-testing example.
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship `PumpkinTest.runFor(Time duration, Subsystem... subsystems)` that ticks periodic → simulationPeriodic → CommandScheduler.run() → SimHooks.stepTiming(0.02) in the correct order. Also `PumpkinTest.runUntil(BooleanSupplier, Time timeout)` for convergence assertions. This is the single missing primitive that blocks small teams from testing closed-loop behavior.

painPoints.problem: The unit-test preamble is undocumented tribal knowledge with inscrutable failure modes
painPoints.evidence: Required steps scattered across three doc sites: `assert HAL.initialize(500, 0)` (WPILib), `AutoCloseable`+`close()` to free HAL allocations (WPILib), `DriverStationSim.setEnabled(true)` + `DriverStation.notifyNewData()` + ~100 ms settle after construction + ~20 ms after each control request (CTRE only — https://v6.docs.ctr-electronics.com/en/latest/docs/api-reference/wpilib-integration/unit-testing.html). Omit the DS enable and actuators read 0.0; omit close() and the *next* test fails with a port-allocation error.
painPoints.libraryFix: A `PumpkinTestBase` / JUnit 5 `@ExtendWith` extension that performs HAL init, DS enable + notify, timing pause, auto-close of all registered `AutoCloseable` subsystems, and vendor settle delays. Reduces the preamble to one annotation and makes the failure modes structurally impossible.

painPoints.problem: Tests run on every build including deploy, so teams disable them permanently and they rot
painPoints.evidence: WPILib docs, verbatim: "By default, Gradle runs the tests whenever robot code is built, including deploys. This will increase deploy time, and failing tests will cause the build and deploy to fail." The documented remedy is the 'Change Skip Tests On Deploy Setting' command — which teams flip once at 2am in the pits and never flip back. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/unit-testing.html
painPoints.libraryFix: Scaffold with tests skipped on deploy but MANDATORY in CI (`./gradlew build` in GitHub Actions). Split fast unit tests from slow sim-integration tests into separate Gradle tasks so the fast suite stays viable pre-deploy. Ship the CI workflow in the template so the safety net lives off the deploy path.

painPoints.problem: maple-sim's 2026 support never left beta, and the repo's own architecture doc is stale
painPoints.evidence: GitHub REST `releases/latest` returns **v0.3.14** (published 2025-08-20, 2025 Reefscape era) because the only 2026 release, **v0.4.0-beta** (published 2026-01-17, "2026 Rebuilt Game Release (Beta)", WPILib 2026.2.1), is flagged prerelease. No further release appeared between Jan 2026 and Aug 2026. Its release notes self-describe as beta with "potential bugs." Meanwhile the repo's CLAUDE.md still names `Arena2025Reefscape` as the current default and makes no mention of 2026, even though the live docs fully document `RebuiltFuelOnField`/`RebuiltFuelOnFly` (https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/rebuilt/). Verified via https://api.github.com/repos/Shenzhen-Robotics-Alliance/maple-sim/releases and .../releases/latest .
painPoints.libraryFix: Treat maple-sim as an OPTIONAL, reflectively-loaded integration behind a stable PumpkinLib interface — never a hard vendordep. If absent or version-incompatible, fall back to plain WPILib mechanism sims with a clear Alert rather than failing to build. Pin the exact tested maple-sim version in docs and re-verify at each kickoff; a small team cannot debug a beta physics engine mid-season.

painPoints.problem: maple-sim's physics-timing knob directly conflicts with AdvantageKit
painPoints.evidence: maple-sim docs, verbatim: "DO NOT override the timing if you are using AdvantageKit, as it only supports 50Hz robots" — https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/using-the-simulated-arena/ . Default is 5 sub-ticks per 0.02 s period. Also verbatim: do not call `SimulatedArena.simulationPeriodic()` on real hardware, "as it will consume roboRIO resources."
painPoints.libraryFix: PumpkinLib should own the arena tick and enforce both rules structurally: gate the call behind `RobotBase.isSimulation()` so it can never run on hardware, and refuse (with a loud, actionable error) any timing override when AdvantageKit is on the classpath. These are exactly the footguns that make a small team conclude 'sim is broken' and abandon it.

painPoints.problem: Limelight has no simulation story at all — a hard wall for teams on the most popular FRC camera
painPoints.evidence: LimelightLib is explicitly documented as a functional, static-method, NetworkTables-only API — "You don't need to create any objects for your Limelights" — with no SimDevice registration, no mock/injection seam, and zero mentions of simulation or testing without hardware (https://docs.limelightvision.io/docs/docs-limelight/apis/limelight-lib). PhotonVision by contrast ships a full `VisionSystemSim`/`PhotonCameraSim`/`SimCameraProperties` stack. I could not find any first-party or credible third-party Limelight sim.
painPoints.libraryFix: Define PumpkinLib's vision input as an interface (pose estimate + timestamp + std-devs + tag IDs) with adapters for PhotonVision, Limelight, and a Sim implementation. Since LimelightHelpers is static, the adapter must wrap it rather than mock it. Then Limelight teams can still simulate — PumpkinLib feeds the sim adapter from maple-sim/`VisionSystemSim` ground truth. Because the static API is untestable by construction, PumpkinLib should recommend PhotonVision as the default in its documented stack and be explicit about why.

painPoints.problem: AdvantageKit's replay power costs an IO-layer rewrite — a tax small teams routinely refuse to pay
painPoints.evidence: Replay requires every hardware interaction behind an IO interface with logged input structs, three implementations per subsystem (Real/Sim/Replay), and strict timestamp discipline (`Timer.getFPGATimestamp()` is not replay-safe; https://docs.advantagekit.org/theory/deterministic-timestamps/). AdvantageKit's own docs state it "requires Java" and "relies on proper IO layer implementation." Meanwhile WPILib's Epilogue gets you logging from a single `@Logged` annotation with no restructuring.
painPoints.libraryFix: Make PumpkinLib IO-shaped BY DEFAULT so replay is available without a rewrite, but never require AdvantageKit. Best-of-both: Epilogue-friendly types out of the box (works immediately, zero ceremony), with the IO seam already in place for teams that later want replay. Consider generating Real+Sim implementations from one mechanism declaration to collapse the 3x implementation tax that is the actual reason small teams bounce off AdvantageKit.

painPoints.problem: Desktop/simulation support is off by default and can crash on vendor libraries
painPoints.evidence: WPILib docs warn verbatim: "Enabling desktop/simulation support can have unintended consequences. Not all vendors will support this option, and code that uses their libraries may even crash when attempting to run simulation!" Requires flipping `includeDesktopSupport = true` in build.gradle or a command-palette toggle. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/introduction.html
painPoints.libraryFix: PumpkinLib's project template ships with desktop support pre-enabled and a documented, verified vendordep set known to work in sim. Add a `pumpkinDoctor` Gradle task that checks the classpath for vendordeps lacking desktop artifacts and reports them before the team wastes an evening on a native-load crash.

painPoints.problem: CI docker image tag drifts silently from the WPILib year
painPoints.evidence: The official CI docs still show `wpilib/roborio-cross-ubuntu:2025-22.04` while documenting 2026 usage, noting the 2025 images remain correct for 2026 because dependencies did not change between those years. That coincidence will NOT hold for 2027 (Java 25, new toolchain, Systemcore). https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/advanced-gradlerio/robot-code-ci.html
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship the workflow with the image tag as a single documented variable and a comment tying it to PumpkinLib's supported WPILib version. Have `pumpkinDoctor` warn when the local WPILib version and the CI image year diverge.

painPoints.problem: WPILib still ships no swerve drivetrain physics sim
painPoints.evidence: `DifferentialDrivetrainSim` is the only drivetrain sim in `edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.simulation`, and it is the sole simulator that does NOT derive from `LinearSystemSim`. The physics-sim doc source served under /en/2027/ still reads "Swerve support for simulation is in the works" — https://docs.wpilib.org/en/2027/_sources/docs/software/wpilib-tools/robot-simulation/physics-sim.rst.txt . Teams must use maple-sim (beta for 2026) or CTRE's `SimSwerveDrivetrain` (CTRE-only, and had an Acceleration-signal regression fixed only in 26.50.0-alpha-1 on 2026/06/12).
painPoints.libraryFix: Genuine gap PumpkinLib can own: a vendor-neutral swerve sim that models per-module dynamics and chassis kinematics, usable without maple-sim and without locking to CTRE. At minimum, provide a unified facade over CTRE `SimSwerveDrivetrain` and maple-sim `SwerveDriveSimulation` so drivetrain code is written once.

painPoints.problem: No standard self-test / health-check framework exists; the Alert API is explicitly unstable
painPoints.evidence: The signals exist but are scattered — `RobotController.getCANStatus()/isBrownedOut()/getFaultCount3V3()/getCommsDisableCount()`, PowerDistribution per-channel currents, Phoenix `isConnected()/getStickyFault_*()/clearStickyFaults()`, CANcoder magnet health — with no aggregation layer anywhere. And WPILib's own Alert docs state the API is "new for 2025" and "likely to change in future seasons to facilitate deeper integration with the robot control system" (https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/release/java/edu/wpi/first/wpilibj/Alert.html).
painPoints.libraryFix: `PumpkinHealth` registry: devices self-register checks, results aggregate into grouped WPILib Alerts (rendered by Elastic's Alerts widget) plus a one-button 'run full self-test' command for the pits. Isolate the Alert API behind a PumpkinLib facade so the documented instability becomes an internal migration, not a breaking change for users. Test the health logic itself using REVLib's `SparkSimFaultManager` fault injection.

painPoints.problem: 2027 breaks essentially every API name PumpkinLib would depend on
painPoints.evidence: Confirmed by diffing the SAME example file across tags: v2026.2.1 uses `edu.wpi.first.wpilibj.examples...`, `DoubleSolenoid.Value.kReverse`, `PneumaticsModuleType.CTREPCM`, `simMotor.getSpeed()`; v2027.0.0-alpha-6 uses `org.wpilib.examples...`, `org.wpilib.hardware.hal.HAL`, `org.wpilib.simulation.PWMMotorControllerSim`, `DoubleSolenoid.Value.REVERSE`, `PneumaticsModuleType.CTRE_PCM`, `simMotor.getThrottle()`. Plus: `robotInit()` removed, `MotorController.set()` → `setThrottle()`, unified `Gamepad` replaces `XboxController`/`PS4Controller`, NT3 removed, Commands v2 deprecated alongside new `org.wpilib.commands3`, Shuffleboard/SmartDashboard/PathWeaver/RobotBuilder deleted, mutable Java units removed, `MathUtil.clamp()` → `Math.clamp()`, `Rotation2d.value` field removed, geometry classes now final, "Test" mode renamed "Utility". https://docs.wpilib.org/en/2027/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html and https://docs.wpilib.org/en/2027/docs/yearly-overview/removed-features.html
painPoints.libraryFix: Decide the target NOW. Recommended: build PumpkinLib's public API in PumpkinLib's own namespace with WPILib types appearing only at the boundary, so the 2027 port is a mostly-mechanical internal change. Avoid re-exporting WPILib enums/constants that get renamed. Do NOT build anything on Shuffleboard/SmartDashboard/NT3 (all deleted). Note the WPILib VS Code importer assists the `edu.wpi.first`→`org.wpilib` migration on project import — but that helps user code, not a published library.

painPoints.problem: Geometry/pose mismatch between physics sim and odometry is a common, confusing first-run failure
painPoints.evidence: Chief Delphi discussion of maple-sim reports a user who found setup "very easy" but then hit a problem where "the physics simulations and odometry didn't align" — https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/maple-sim-alpha-bringing-robot-simulations-to-the-next-level-with-physics-engines/473238 . maple-sim added automatic pose reset on odometry reset in v0.3.3 specifically to address this class of bug. CAVEAT: chiefdelphi.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so this rests on search-result snippets plus the release notes, not full thread text.
painPoints.libraryFix: PumpkinLib should own the ground-truth↔estimate relationship: auto-publish both `SimulatedArena` ground-truth pose and the estimator pose to AdvantageScope on distinct keys, and expose a `PumpkinSim.poseError()` metric assertable in tests. Wire odometry reset to arena pose reset in one place so the two can never silently diverge.

constraints: **Pick a WPILib target year explicitly and design for the 2027 break.** 2026 = `edu.wpi.first.*` (stable, 2026.2.x); 2027 = `org.wpilib.*` (alpha; tag v2027.0.0-alpha-6 exists as of this research). These are source-incompatible. Renames verified by diffing allwpilib's own IntakeTest.java across tags: `HAL` → `org.wpilib.hardware.hal.HAL`, `PWMMotorControllerSim.getSpeed()` → `getThrottle()`, `DoubleSolenoid.Value.kReverse` → `REVERSE`, `PneumaticsModuleType.CTREPCM` → `CTRE_PCM`. Keep WPILib types at PumpkinLib's boundary, not woven through its public API. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/2027/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html

**Do not build on anything Systemcore removes.** No relay, analog output, analog gyro, SPI or SPI IMUs (ADIS16448/16470, ADXRS450, ADXL345), DMA, Counter, AnalogTrigger, DigitalGlitchFilter, interrupts, ultrasonic, servo, or built-in accelerometer. NetworkTables v3 is gone (NT4 only). Systemcore ADDS multiple CAN buses, Smart IO, an onboard IMU (with sim support), and an Expansion Hub — a multi-CAN-bus-aware device abstraction is future-proofing, not over-engineering. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/2027/docs/yearly-overview/removed-features.html

**Do not build on removed tooling.** Shuffleboard, SmartDashboard, PathWeaver, and RobotBuilder are all deleted for 2027 (deprecated in 2026). Target Elastic (driver dashboard) + AdvantageScope (analysis) only; PathPlanner/Choreo/Bline for paths. Note the Alert API publishes under `/SmartDashboard/<Group>` — that NT *path* persists even though the SmartDashboard *application* is gone.

**Replay-safety is a hard API constraint if replay is ever a goal.** Never call `Timer.getFPGATimestamp()` in control logic — it bypasses AdvantageKit's per-cycle timestamp injection and is not replayable. Use `Timer.getTimestamp()`, or better, accept an injectable clock so tests and replay can drive time. Prefer timestamps carried with the measurement (NT4, Phoenix 6 signals) over robot-side clock reads. https://docs.advantagekit.org/theory/deterministic-timestamps/

**50 Hz is effectively mandatory.** AdvantageKit only supports 50 Hz robots, and maple-sim's docs explicitly forbid overriding simulation timings when AdvantageKit is present. PumpkinLib must not require a non-20 ms loop period, and must not silently change it. https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/using-the-simulated-arena/

**All simulation code must be strippable and no-op on real hardware.** Gate on `RobotBase.isSimulation()`. maple-sim docs explicitly warn that calling `SimulatedArena.simulationPeriodic()` on hardware consumes roboRIO resources. Sim must add zero measurable loop time on the real robot.

**Everything must run headless in the CI container.** Target `wpilib/roborio-cross-ubuntu:<year>-22.04` on ubuntu-22.04 with no display, no hardware, no network. Practical consequences: `HAL.initialize(500, 0)` is required in every test; PhotonVision OpenCV stream rendering must be disabled (`enableRawStream(false)`, `enableProcessedStream(false)`) since it is documented as computationally expensive; and no test may depend on wall-clock timing.

**Every simulated device must be closed.** HAL port allocations leak across JUnit tests; the official example implements `AutoCloseable` and closes in `@AfterEach`. Any PumpkinLib object owning a HAL resource must be `AutoCloseable`, and the test harness must close them automatically.

**Vendor sim support is uneven and must degrade gracefully.** Phoenix 6 (deep), REVLib (good), PhotonVision (excellent), Limelight (none), maple-sim (2026 = beta only). WPILib warns some vendor libraries crash outright under simulation. PumpkinLib must build and run with any subset present, reporting missing capability via Alerts rather than failing to compile or crashing on native load.

**Java 25 / C++23 for 2027; Commands v3 requires Java 21+ continuations.** Commands v3 (`org.wpilib.commands3`, coroutine-based) explicitly could not ship earlier because the roboRIO JVM lacked the needed features. Commands v2 is deprecated but present in 2027. PumpkinLib should avoid hard-coupling its public API to either command framework — expose behavior via factories/suppliers that can produce v2 or v3 commands.

**Respect the units API direction.** WPILib 2026 added unit-based method overloads; 2027 REMOVES mutable Java units (Systemcore has enough RAM). Use immutable `Measure` types (`Volts.of`, `Meters.of`, `Amps.of`) in PumpkinLib's public API — this is both the documented direction and the main defense against the gear-ratio/unit-conversion bugs that plague sim glue.

**maple-sim must be optional, not load-bearing.** Its 2026 support is prerelease-only (v0.4.0-beta, 2026-01-17) with no stable 2026 release as of Aug 2026, and the repo's own CLAUDE.md is stale relative to its docs. Reflectively load it behind a stable PumpkinLib interface with a plain-WPILib-sim fallback; pin and re-verify the tested version at kickoff.

**Cite-and-verify caveats on this research.** (1) chiefdelphi.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches, so all Chief Delphi claims here rest on search snippets, not full thread text — verify community sentiment manually. (2) WPILib 2027 is in ALPHA; its changelog is explicitly subject to change and should be re-checked at 2027 kickoff. (3) `CANStatus`'s exact fields were not enumerated in the fetched Javadoc — confirm before depending on `percentBusUtilization` et al. (4) I found no evidence of any Limelight simulation support; absence of evidence here is strong but not proof.

TIMING IS THE DOMINANT CONSTRAINT: 2027 is a hard break, not an increment. WPILib 2027 (docs.wpilib.org/en/2027/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html) renames Java packages `edu.wpi.first` -> `org.wpilib` and C++ `frc::` -> `wpi::`, requires Java 25 / C++23, upgrades GradleRIO to Gradle 9.4.1 with ZGC default, and targets SystemCore (roboRIO gone). A PumpkinLib written against 2026 APIs will not compile in 2027. Decide NOW whether PumpkinLib targets 2026 (roboRIO, one-season shelf life) or 2027 (SystemCore, org.wpilib). 2027 kickoff is Jan 9, 2027; game is BIOCORE (firstinspires.org/programs/frc/game-and-season).

FIELD COORDINATE ORIGIN MOVES IN 2027. Peter Johnson (WPILib lead) on Chief Delphi: "Math: field pose origin/orientation – (0,0) is center of field, scoring table at top (180 degree rotation from today)" (chiefdelphi.com/t/programming-library-changes-for-2027/519900). Any PumpkinLib helper that hardcodes alliance flipping, field dimensions, or blue-origin assumptions must be written against an abstraction, not constants. Flipping becomes a simple negation under center-origin.

DO NOT REIMPLEMENT: swerve kinematics/odometry (WPILib + CTRE SwerveDrivetrain + YAGSL), trajectory generation (PathPlannerLib 2026.1.2, Choreo 2026.0.3), vision pose estimation (PhotonLib 2026.3.4, LimelightHelpers MegaTag2), motor control primitives (Phoenix 6 26.3.0, REVLib 2026.0.5), log replay (AdvantageKit v26.0.2), log visualization (AdvantageScope v26.0.2, bundled in WPILib installer), driver dashboard (Elastic 2026.1.2), or system identification (WPILib SysIdRoutine). Every one of these is mature and free. A new library that competes here will lose.

NETWORKTABLES 4 ONLY from 2027; NT3 is fully removed (docs.wpilib.org/en/2027/docs/yearly-overview/removed-features.html). Shuffleboard and SmartDashboard are removed. Any dashboard integration must target NT4 struct/protobuf publishing consumed by Elastic and AdvantageScope.

HARDWARE APIS REMOVED IN 2027: Relay, AnalogOutput, AnalogGyro, SPI (and all SPI IMUs — ADIS16448, ADIS16470, ADXL345, ADXRS450), DigitalGlitchFilter, AnalogTrigger, DMA, Counter, Ultrasonic, Interrupts, Servo. `XboxController`/`PS4Controller`/`PS5Controller`/`StadiaController` collapse into one `Gamepad` class. `robotInit()` removed (use constructor). `MotorController::set()` -> `setThrottle()`, `StopMotor()` -> `Disable()`. `RamseteCommand`/`RamseteController` removed (use LTV Unicycle). `PIDCommand`/`ProfiledPIDCommand`/`TrapezoidProfileCommand` removed. `MathUtil.clamp()` -> `Math.clamp()`. Rotation2d `value` field removed.

MUTABLE UNITS ARE REMOVED IN 2027 ("Mutable Java units: Replaced by immutable units", removed-features page). Do not build a PumpkinLib API around `MutableMeasure`/`MutDistance` for GC avoidance — that escape hatch disappears. Design for immutable `Measure` (Distance, LinearVelocity, Angle, etc.) and accept the allocation, or use raw doubles internally at the hot path.

COMMANDS V2 SURVIVES INTO 2027 alongside v3. Peter Johnson: "Commands v3 (but v2 is still available)". Commands v3 is Java-only (C++ has no production coroutines; robotpy will differ). PumpkinLib should target v2 for portability and treat v3 as an optional adapter, OR commit to v3 and accept Java-only. Do not require v3 — it is unfinished and controversial (see the coroutine.yield() footgun discussion).

DISTRIBUTION MUST BE A VENDORDEP JSON + MAVEN, not a copy-paste template. Precedent URLs: PathPlannerLib https://3015rangerrobotics.github.io/pathplannerlib/PathplannerLib.json ; ChoreoLib https://choreo.autos/lib/ChoreoLib2026.json ; DogLog https://doglog.dev/vendordep.json ; FrcCatalyst https://tomas-1226.github.io/FrcCatalyst/vendordep/FrcCatalyst.json ; Studica https://dev.studica.com/maven/release/2026/json/Studica-2026.0.0.json ; ReduxLib https://frcsdk.reduxrobotics.com/ReduxLib_2026.json. AdvantageKit's zip-template distribution is a documented usability failure (see painPoints).

LICENSE COMPATIBILITY: AdvantageKit is BSD-3-Clause-style but headed "Copyright (c) 2021-2026 Littleton Robotics. All rights reserved." with a non-endorsement clause (raw.githubusercontent.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/main/LICENSE). YAMS is LGPLv3 per its GitHub page — LGPL in a vendordep is a real consideration for teams. FrcCatalyst is MIT. Pick MIT/BSD for PumpkinLib and avoid hard-linking LGPL code into the distributed jar.

MUST WORK OFFLINE AT COMPETITION. No pit internet is assumed. Anything requiring a web service, code generation server, or dependency resolution at deploy time is disqualified. Choreo's Java constants codegen and Epilogue's annotation processor both run at compile time on the laptop — that is the acceptable pattern.

MUST NOT REQUIRE AdvantageKit. AdvantageKit imposes LoggedRobot + IO-layer discipline as an all-or-nothing architecture and its 2027 status is unclear (docs state "template projects are not currently available for the 2027 alpha versions"; v27.0.0-alpha-4 is restricted to SystemCore alpha teams). PumpkinLib should be usable with plain TimedRobot + Epilogue/DogLog, and *compatible* with AdvantageKit if the team wants it (YAMS explicitly does this: "It just requires the boundary to be at setpoints rather than voltage").

VENDOR NEUTRALITY IS A REAL TRADEOFF, NOT A FREE WIN. Chief Delphi consensus in the FrcCatalyst thread: CTRE-only libraries get deeper features (Motion Magic, FOC, hoot logging, fused CANcoder); vendor-agnostic libraries (YAMS/YAGSL) "lose a lot of the ctre feature" but serve more teams. Whichever PumpkinLib chooses, provide YAMS' escape hatch: allow passing a raw vendor config object through, and do not block use of the vendor's own closed-loop control.

SMALL-TEAM SUCCESSION RISK IS A DESIGN CONSTRAINT, NOT A FOOTNOTE. nstrike (YASS) on Chief Delphi re: BLine: "Projects like MapleSim are waning in support as the developer has graduated and if you don't have a succession plan this may be more of a hindrance for teams that would like to use it for many seasons." PumpkinLib needs a documented maintenance/succession plan and a hard rule that a team can rip it out mid-season without rewriting the robot.

MUST DEGRADE TO PLAIN WPILIB. A small team hitting a bug at 11pm before a competition must be able to bypass PumpkinLib for one subsystem without unwinding the whole codebase. Design as composable helpers over a monolithic framework.

painPoints.problem: Kickoff-week vendor library lag blocks small teams from starting at all. Templates that depend on multiple vendordeps cannot ship until every vendor publishes, and that can be weeks.
painPoints.evidence: AdvantageKit 2026 kickoff thread: jonahb55 said the Spark swerve template "[is] not yet released since they depend on libraries from vendors who have not published 2026 versions" and, asked about the TalonFX template, "Right now we're waiting on PathPlanner to release a 2026 build (ideally also Studica...). I'm not sure what PathPlanner's timeline is." NavX IO implementations were shipped disabled until Studica published. https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/advantagekit-2026-replay-refined/509227
painPoints.libraryFix: PumpkinLib should have ZERO hard vendordep dependencies in its core artifact. Use reflection-free optional integration: compile against interfaces, detect vendor classes at runtime (Class.forName / ServiceLoader), and ship vendor adapters as separate optional artifacts. A team should be able to install PumpkinLib on kickoff day with only WPILib present and add Phoenix/REV/PathPlanner adapters as they land.

painPoints.problem: AdvantageKit's zip-template distribution model is a documented onboarding failure for exactly the teams a small-team library targets.
painPoints.evidence: AfterTen on Chief Delphi: "I don't get how the template projects work... When I look in the repository I see 'template_projects' and inside that then 'sources', 'template'... If I use the 'template' folder and treat it as the root of a robot project... I get an error that a team number cannot be set because it is not a WPILib project." rickmaster: "When trying to build the TalonFX template, I get an error: 'Cannot Build Robot Code since this is not a WPILib project'. All I did was unzip the project and attempt to build." AdvantageKit docs also say "Manually updating projects to 2026 is not recommended due to the risk of subtle breaking changes." https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/advantagekit-2026-replay-refined/509227
painPoints.libraryFix: Distribute as a vendordep, not a template. A team's existing project must keep working after `Install` with zero file moves. If PumpkinLib needs scaffolding, generate it with a WPILib VS Code example project or an annotation processor — never a zip the student has to unpack into the right place.

painPoints.problem: Every team hand-rolls the same tunable-constant plumbing. There are at least six independent, incompatible implementations in the community and none of them is in WPILib for 2026.
painPoints.evidence: Chief Delphi "How are team's implementing adjustable constants" (https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/how-are-teams-implementing-adjustable-constants/507361) surfaced, in one 16-post thread: WPILib Sendables, 6328's `LoggedTunableNumber` (github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/RobotCode2025Public .../util/LoggedTunableNumber.java), DogLog's `DogLog.tunable(...)`, YAMS Live Tuning (yagsl.gitbook.io/yams), Team 340's custom `/Tunables` NT table (bryceroethel), pjreiniger's Preferences-wrapper vendordep, and CTRE Tuner X device configs. bryceroethel: "there's currently a PR targeting the 2027 release of WPILib that includes a Tunables API" — i.e. still not shipped as of 2026.
painPoints.libraryFix: A first-class Tunable primitive is the single highest-value, lowest-risk thing PumpkinLib can ship. Requirements from the thread: (1) compiles to a constant when tuning mode is off (6328's pattern), so zero competition overhead; (2) persists to disk on the controller so values survive redeploy/power-cycle (pjreiniger's ask); (3) publishes under a single NT root readable by Elastic AND AdvantageScope tuning mode; (4) works for PID gains, feedforward, AND setpoints; (5) supports per-robot values (practice vs comp bot). Design the API so it can be re-pointed at the WPILib 2027 Tunables API when that lands.

painPoints.problem: SmartDashboard/telemetry causes loop overruns on small-team robots, and the team's instinct is to log LESS — which destroys their ability to debug.
painPoints.evidence: brainiac on Chief Delphi: "Is there a way to do this without using smart dashboard? When we use smart dashboard, our loop times almost always overrun, so we are trying to limit our use of smart dashboard." https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/how-are-teams-implementing-adjustable-constants/507361 . Epilogue's own docs warn that overhead "comes from calling expensive methods (especially repeated CAN bus queries)" and that `Epilogue.bind()` runs at a half-phase offset from the 50Hz loop, desynchronizing logged values from control values.
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship a telemetry policy layer, not just telemetry: per-signal rate limiting, a competition/debug importance switch (Epilogue has `minimumImportance` but teams don't wire it), CAN signal caching so the same `getPosition()` is read once per loop and reused by both control and logging, and a built-in loop-time budget alert that names the offending subsystem. This is a genuine gap — nobody ships it.

painPoints.problem: Epilogue's annotation-based logging has hard structural limits that force teams back to manual logging exactly where it hurts.
painPoints.evidence: WPILib docs (docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/telemetry/robot-telemetry-with-annotations.html): cannot log static members, private methods, or methods taking arguments; null values throw NPE into the error handler because "log data cannot represent nulls"; "Logged fields use their declared type, not runtime subtypes" — so an interface-typed field (i.e. every IO-layer field) logs via the interface, not the concrete impl; vendor types need a hand-written `@CustomLoggerFor` `ClassSpecificLogger`. 2026 improved this somewhat (superclass field/method logging via reflection, protobuf support, backend time/memory optimization) but the core limits remain.
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship pre-built `@CustomLoggerFor` loggers for TalonFX/TalonFXS/SparkMax/SparkFlex/CANcoder/CANrange/Pigeon2/PhotonCamera so a small team gets rich per-device telemetry for free. This is pure grunt work no small team will ever do, it is exactly the "depend, don't reimplement" sweet spot, and it composes with Epilogue rather than replacing it.

painPoints.problem: Swerve bring-up remains the single biggest small-team failure mode, and the failure is almost never in the math — it is in configuration, IDs, offsets, and inversions.
painPoints.evidence: Live example: "URGENT HELP- Swerve Code (AdvantageKit Spark Template)" — EceSoylu: "it is our first year in FRC as programmers. We can't really figure it out trough the documents... We have to make the robot move and turn perfectly... so that the team won't die this year." The community's diagnostic reply (BobbyVanNess) is a pure checklist of *configuration* faults: "check your defined x and y positions of each swerve module, check all of your devices in phoenix tuner... blink them to identify one by one and verify they match how they're defined in your code. Make sure they're up to date on firmware and don't ignore any issues or duplicate ID's. Set your wheels straight (bevels facing the same way) and verify your offsets are all correct. Wiggle one wheel at a time and verify that the encoder value you expect to see change changes." https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/urgent-help-swerve-code-advantagekit-spark-template/515511
painPoints.libraryFix: Encode BobbyVanNess's checklist as EXECUTABLE CODE. A `PumpkinLib.verify()` / bring-up wizard command that at robot init: enumerates configured CAN IDs, reports duplicates and missing devices as Alerts, checks firmware versions, and offers an interactive per-module routine (drive one module, confirm which wheel moved; spin one wheel, confirm which encoder changed; auto-capture steer offsets with wheels aligned). Nobody ships this. It directly addresses the documented #1 failure. This is the strongest differentiating feature identified in this research.

painPoints.problem: There is no standard pre-match self-test / health check, so small teams discover a dead motor or unplugged CANcoder on the field.
painPoints.evidence: FrcCatalyst advertises "health check-based fault monitoring" and "temperature cutoff, limit-switch auto-zero" as headline differentiators (tomas-1226.github.io/FrcCatalyst), which indicates the need is real and unmet in WPILib. WPILib's Alert API exists (`Alert`, `AlertType` kError/kWarning/kInfo, published to `/SmartDashboard/<Group>`, docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/telemetry/persistent-alerts.html) but WPILib ships zero built-in alerts — the team must author every condition themselves.
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship a library of pre-authored Alerts that light up automatically: CAN device not present, CAN utilization high, firmware mismatch, motor over-temperature, encoder not moving while commanded, battery sag under threshold, loop overrun, vision camera disconnected, gyro not calibrated. Plus a `SystemCheckCommand` that exercises each mechanism through its range and reports pass/fail. Both build on stock WPILib Alert — no reinvention, huge value.

painPoints.problem: WPILib's units library has aliasing and allocation footguns, and the workaround (MutableMeasure) is being deleted in 2027.
painPoints.evidence: WPILib docs (docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/basic-programming/java-units.html) warn: "if we run the `calculateDelta` method a few times" with mutable inputs, deltas become zero because "the `m_lastDistance` field is a reference to the *same* `MutDistance` object as the input"; "Default operations allocate new objects"; `PerUnit`/`MultUnit` need `ofNative()` not `of()`. Meanwhile the 2027 removed-features page lists "Mutable Java units: Replaced by immutable units".
painPoints.libraryFix: Take a position and enforce it: PumpkinLib's public API uses immutable `Measure` types (Distance, Angle, LinearVelocity, Voltage) at configuration boundaries only, and raw doubles in per-loop hot paths. Document the boundary explicitly. Do not expose MutableMeasure anywhere — it is a 2027 landmine.

painPoints.problem: Commands v3's coroutine model introduces a silent, uncheckable footgun that will disproportionately hurt small teams.
painPoints.evidence: catrix on Chief Delphi: "if I somehow forget to add this single line [coroutine.yield()], MY ROBOT WILL EXPLODE. And I get absolutely zero warning or error about it during compile or deploy... It's also very hard to explain coroutine.fork() and coroutine.yield() to a junior programmer." SamCarlberg (WPILib) conceded: "Yep. That's the glaring footgun with the coroutine-first approach; there's no way to check at compile time so it's up to the programmer to be aware of it. A watchdog will be necessary..." https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wpilib-commands-v3-imperative-function-bodies-with-coroutines/500699
painPoints.libraryFix: Do not build PumpkinLib's core on Commands v3. Build on v2 (which Peter Johnson confirms remains available in 2027), and if v3 support is added, ship the missing watchdog: a scheduler wrapper that detects a command exceeding its time budget without yielding and raises a named Alert identifying the command. Oblarg's framing is the safe one: treat v3 as "a more expressive alternative to the current ProxyCommand", not the default.

painPoints.problem: Sim-vs-real divergence: teams write two code paths and the sim path rots, so pre-season/offseason work doesn't transfer.
painPoints.evidence: YASS markets its core value as "your team to rapidly prototype and develop seamlessly in simulation and the robot with the same code" (yetanothersoftwaresuite.com), and YAMS exposes `simIterate()` with physics models built in. maple-sim exists precisely because WPILib sim can't model game-piece interaction. nstrike on the value: "The best part is you don't have to have a robot with you to test this. Its a huge timesaver!" — which is the defining constraint of a small team with limited robot access.
painPoints.libraryFix: Make simulation a non-optional, zero-config property of every PumpkinLib mechanism: if you declare gearing, mass, and moment of inertia in the config, the WPILib physics model (ElevatorSim/SingleJointedArmSim/FlywheelSim/DCMotorSim) is wired automatically with no second code path. FrcCatalyst and YAMS both do this and both cite it as their top selling point. Optionally bridge to maple-sim for game-piece physics — but only optionally (see maintenance risk below).

painPoints.problem: Community libraries carry succession risk that small teams cannot absorb, and maple-sim is the cautionary example.
painPoints.evidence: nstrike (YASS maintainer) on Chief Delphi: "Projects like MapleSim are waning in support as the developer has graduated and if you don't have a succession plan this may be more of a hindrance for teams that would like to use it for many seasons." maple-sim's own 2026 release is labeled "This is a beta version of the library, bugs and glitches may exist" with latest v0.4.0-beta (github.com/Shenzhen-Robotics-Alliance/maple-sim/releases). BLine is explicitly "built by Team 2638 Rebel Robotics, by students for students" with development started June 2025.
painPoints.libraryFix: Treat this as a marketing and architecture requirement: publish a succession plan, keep the dependency graph shallow (WPILib + optional vendor adapters only), and never make a beta third-party library (maple-sim) a required dependency. Version PumpkinLib by season (2027.x.y) so teams can pin.

painPoints.problem: Multi-robot constants (practice bot vs competition bot) is a universal need with no standard solution.
painPoints.evidence: 3061-lib's README calls it out as a headline feature: "supports multiple robots with different configurations, which is useful for supporting multiple physical robots with the same code base (e.g., a practice bot and a competition bot)" (github.com/HuskieRobotics/3061-lib). On CD, githubAnish recommends a base-constants-class-plus-subclass pattern and pjreiniger's vendordep persists Preferences to disk "Also very useful if you have two robots that need different constants."
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship robot-identity resolution (roboRIO/SystemCore serial number or a jumper/DIO strap) plus a constants-layering mechanism, integrated with the Tunable system so a value tuned on the practice bot can be promoted to the comp bot's persisted store. Small lift, universally needed, nobody standardizes it.

painPoints.problem: PathPlannerLib deliberately froze in 2026, leaving a one-season window where autonomous tooling is stable but stagnant — and it will change for SystemCore.
painPoints.evidence: mjansen (PathPlanner author, username kreeve) announcing the 2026 release: "There have been no major changes of note this year besides the addition of the 2026 field image. My plan is to hold off on major changes for the 2027 switch to SystemCore." https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/advantagekit-2026-replay-refined/509227 . Latest is v2026.1.2 (Jan 12, 2026), whose only change was fixing the 2026 field image scale.
painPoints.libraryFix: Do not wrap PathPlannerLib's API surface tightly — it will move for 2027. Wrap only the four things AutoBuilder actually needs from a drivetrain (pose supplier, pose reset, robot-relative ChassisSpeeds supplier, ChassisSpeeds consumer) behind a PumpkinLib drivetrain interface, so swapping PathPlanner <-> Choreo <-> BLine is a one-line change for the team.

painPoints.problem: Teams still hand-write the Choreo/PathPlanner glue and the alliance-flip logic, and get it wrong.
painPoints.evidence: Choreo 2026.0.0 added Java constants codegen specifically because "trajectories were loaded by providing the String name of the trajectory, but there was no compile-time check to ensure the referenced trajectories actually existed" and "Many teams asked for a way to access the defined pose variables from robot code, and several developed systems to parse the .chor file at runtime" (github.com/SleipnirGroup/Choreo/releases). PathPlanner AutoBuilder requires the user to supply a red-alliance boolean supplier by hand.
painPoints.libraryFix: Choreo already solved the codegen half — depend on it. The remaining gap PumpkinLib can close: a single correct, tested alliance/origin abstraction that works for both 2026 blue-origin and 2027 center-origin conventions, so teams write `Field.flipIfRed(pose)` once and it keeps working across the coordinate change.

patterns.name: IO-layer hardware abstraction (AdvantageKit pattern)
patterns.whatItDoes: Splits each subsystem into a plain-data `Inputs` struct, an `IO` interface with `updateInputs(inputs)` plus setter methods, and vendor-specific `IOTalonFX`/`IOSpark`/`IOSim` implementations. The subsystem logic reads only from the inputs struct, so the entire robot state can be deterministically replayed from a log in simulation.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.advantagekit.org/ ; templates at https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/releases (v26.0.2, 2026-03-19). Adopted by 3061-lib (https://github.com/HuskieRobotics/3061-lib), FRC 1678 C2026-Public, FRC 2910. AdvantageKit reports 600+ teams in 2025, 200+ using its swerve templates (https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/advantagekit-2026-replay-refined/509227).
patterns.libraryValue: This is the single most-copied architecture in FRC and PumpkinLib should be shaped so it composes with it rather than fighting it. AdvantageKit already owns replay; do not rebuild it. The gap: the IO-layer split costs a small team ~3x the boilerplate per subsystem and there is no code generation for it. An annotation processor that generates the `Inputs` class and the `@AutoLog` plumbing from a single annotated interface, and that degrades to direct calls when AdvantageKit is absent, is high-value and non-duplicative.

patterns.name: Declarative mechanism config builder (YAMS / FrcCatalyst pattern)
patterns.whatItDoes: A single builder describes a mechanism's physical reality (motor type, CAN IDs, gear ratio, drum radius/length, mass/MOI, soft limits, current limits) and its control (PID slots, feedforward incl. gravity term, Motion Magic or ProfiledPID constraints, named positions). The library derives closed-loop control, unit conversion, soft/hard limits, a WPILib physics sim model, telemetry, and SysId routines from that one declaration.
patterns.whereSeen: YAMS: https://github.com/Yet-Another-Software-Suite/YAMS , https://yagsl.gitbook.io/yams (mechanisms: Arm, Elevator, Pivot/turret/hood, Flywheel, SwerveDrive; LGPLv3). FrcCatalyst v1.8.0: https://tomas-1226.github.io/FrcCatalyst/ (LinearMechanism, RotationalMechanism, FlywheelMechanism, RollerMechanism, WinchMechanism, ClawMechanism, DifferentialWristMechanism, PneumaticMechanism, Superstructure; MIT; WPILib 2026.2.1 + Phoenix 6 26.1.1). Claimed reduction: elevator with gravity FF ~150 lines -> ~8 lines.
patterns.libraryValue: This is the proven core value proposition for small teams and the pattern PumpkinLib should adopt. Two independent projects converged on it in 2026 and both are being used in competition, which validates demand. The differentiators still open: (a) FrcCatalyst is CTRE-only, (b) YAMS is LGPLv3 and vendor-agnostic at the cost of vendor-specific features, (c) neither has a strong bring-up/verification story, (d) neither is designed for the 2027 org.wpilib break. PumpkinLib can win on 2027-first design + verification tooling rather than on the builder itself.

patterns.name: Vendor-normalizing SmartMotorController with a config escape hatch
patterns.whatItDoes: One `SmartMotorController` interface over Phoenix 6 TalonFX/TalonFXS, REVLib SparkMax/SparkFlex, and ThriftyNova, normalizing configuration, closed-loop setpoints, feedforward, motion profiles, and telemetry. Crucially it does NOT hide the vendor: teams can pass a raw vendor config object through, and can keep using the vendor's own onboard closed-loop control.
patterns.whereSeen: YAMS `yams.motorcontrollers.SmartMotorController` / `SmartMotorControllerConfig` / `yams.motorcontrollers.remote.TalonFXSWrapper`. Docs: https://yagsl.gitbook.io/yams (Passing a Vendor Config; CTRE-Specific Notes). nstrike on CD: "We have an escape hatch for every vendor allowing users to pass in whatever vendor config thats applicable. We also don't prevent the user from using the vendors SMC if they want to."
patterns.libraryValue: The escape-hatch design is the key lesson and PumpkinLib should copy it verbatim as a rule. Community criticism of over-abstraction is specific and worth heeding — tcrvo on CD: "This encourages overabstraction if the shared namespace becomes anything more than a way to keep the import list shorter... subtle differences pile up." Also note the honest limitation nstrike names: setpoint caching breaks when the user drives the vendor SMC directly, "most SMC's dont expose the previous setpoint."
